tools.name: get_started
tools.description: REQUIRED FIRST STEP before building any HELIX Instant world. Returns the complete project recipe. Pass kind="character" for a world with a player character in ANY camera framing — all built on the humanoid-character system. Pass kind="multiplayer" for a world where players share a space and/or a game — presence PLUS declarative game logic (scores, teams, entities, physics, turns); returns the multiplayer HUB that routes to 15 worked templates + the multiplayer-logic DSL (you write no server code). Pass kind="scene" for a bare scene with no character. Omit kind to get the decision guide. If the world SELLS anything (a shop, currency, passes, cosmetics, tips, unlocks), that is in-world purchases and layers onto any of these — see read_doc({name:"purchases"}) and read_template({name:"world-shop"}).

kind.description: "character" = humanoid-character world; "multiplayer" = shared world (presence + declarative game logic; the hub + 15 templates + the DSL); "scene" = bare world; "vehicle" = make, convert or publish a drivable VEHICLE item (car, kart, truck — from a real-world model name, a game mod, a downloaded model, a concept image, or from scratch) or its add-ons; "avatar" = make, convert, fix or publish an AVATAR item (a playable character body from a VRM, a generated character, a game model or a robot), including hair/cloth/tail physics bones; omit for the decision guide

tools.name: read_doc
tools.description: Read a HELIX Instant reference document: "bridge" (the plugin-driven external content import workflow), "continuum" (AI-native semantic Scenes, exact-CID Packages/Builds, resume and publication policy), "character-world", "character-animation" (authoring CUSTOM character gestures as JSON keyframe poses — for SHORT SIMPLE upper-body-led motion only: player actions, stances, one-shot accents, additive overlays. NOT dances, fight moves or acrobatics — no root motion, foot planting or weight shift. Carries the axis table, compile-time ik keys for hand-position goals + runtime reach/gaze IK (≥ 0.2.15), why rotations chaining breaks joint-space posing, and the headless pose evaluator), "avatar-face" (WHETHER A CHARACTER CAN MOVE ITS MOUTH AT ALL — the helix/avatar-face@1 manifest must ride the GLB at IMPORT time; nothing at runtime can add one later and an avatar without it is permanently mute with no error raised anywhere. The viseme15 > vowel5 > jaw > none capability ladder, the receiver-local boundary — no facial weight is ever networked — why mp.attachVoice() is the entire world-side integration, the automatic VRM path, when a faceMap is REQUIRED (a VRoid model exported as GLB rather than VRM imports mute), bone-vs-morph jaw targets, why add-ons never carry faces, and the honest limits: Face V1 is 0.3-line only, and the stock Base Female ships with NO face channels), "locomotion-clip-spec" (LOCOMOTION PACKS: authoring the replacement movement clip set a player equips as a character add-on — the pack format (anims/clip-meta.json + one GLB per clip), the gait-only clip vocabulary (the core nine, the strafe rings, turn-in-place), strideSpeed as a MEASUREMENT with its per-clip bands and the walk < run < sprint ladder, the canonical skeleton contract, and the loader's per-clip failure behaviour; partial packs down to one clip are valid products), "shooter-worlds" (GUNS: the gun-control ability contract, weapon profiles, FX/hit systems + the frame-order contract, health/death/ragdoll, replica stances, published gun definitions, and explosive weapons — rockets and grenades as published items plus the world rules their blast needs — read it for ANY world where players shoot), "npc-world" (NPCS: a shopkeeper, quest giver, guard or a monster that hunts the player — an NPC is a Character whose driver is your behaviour instead of the keyboard. NpcScene and the stand/physics body tiers, AIDriver behaviours and the two ordering rules whose failures are silent, the attack doctrine, NavGrid pathfinding and its honest v1 limits, InteractionSpots prompts, Vault characters as NPC bodies, and the multiplayer handoff to humanoidEntities), "multiplayer-world" (shared-presence worlds: the CharacterMultiplayer facade, typed state accessors + the single-player→multiplayer conversion guide), "multiplayer-logic" (the declarative game-logic DSL: declared state, when/if/then rules, entities, zones, timers, state machine, collections, ownership, the weaponDamage op), "bring-your-world" (adopt HELIX in an EXISTING three.js project, staged: become a world → adopt the character → go multiplayer), "lighting-world" (the platform lighting path — the visual runtime that owns the renderer/sky/sun/grade, the public/helix.visuals.json contract, the baked-vs-dynamic decision tree, the publish-time bake via bake_world_lighting, quality tiers, converting a hand-lit world, and the opt-out for worlds with their own visual style), "world-look" (making a raw world LOOK good — fix defects before taste: the asset-truth import checklist for scale/metalness/normals/colorspaces/alpha, geometry-first sun aim, consuming platform materials correctly with per-axis repeat and multiplier semantics, texture hygiene — mips inside the KTX2, minFilter, textures-before-AA — scene assembly, composition, and judging your own captures), "scene-performance" (first-build and final measurable optimization: exact Scene resource scope, authored versus submitted geometry, material/Palette and delivery counters, estimated reference-budget utilization, receipt limits, and matched fullscreen visual QA), "sdk" (full @helix3/helix-sdk API), "items" (Standard/Collectible definitions, Marketplace/World distributions, shell-mediated Claim/Buy and resale policy), "purchases" (SELLING world-local consumables/effects — registration, entitlements + consume, reload recovery and room-side rules), "manifest" (every helix.json field + bundle rules), "publishing" (pipeline, login, error semantics), "screenshots" (declaring hero shots, the capture/inspect/attach workflow, the thumbnail/preview slots), "world-inspect" (measuring world layout as data: the world.ready integration, the placement checks, measure-then-look, findings as measurements not verdicts), "upgrades" (existing-world migration ledger: stale pins, missing capabilities, step-by-step fixes), "catalog" (platform systems/abilities/asset-packs), "world-recipe" (bare-scene worlds with no character), "terrain" (GROUND for a scene world: the --terrain scaffold flag, generating or importing a heightfield, the six presets, inspect before you publish, and the lighting policy), "vehicles" (the HELIX VEHICLE CONTRACT for making or converting a drivable vehicle item and its add-ons: mesh parts and naming, pivots/axes/units, seats, materials, budgets, the landV2 physics fields and how to derive them from real specs, audio, add-on anchoring, publish and the visual verification it requires — get_started({kind:"vehicle"}) for the workflow).

tools.name: read_skill
tools.description: Read a first-party HELIX skill — the WORKFLOW and judgment for a kind of job, where read_doc holds the contract. Skills: helix-assets, helix-avatar-qa, helix-avatars, helix-gauntlet, helix-multiplayer, helix-vehicles, helix-world-build, helix-world-director, helix-world-qa. Omit reference to read the skill's SKILL.md (it lists its references); pass reference to read one reference file, e.g. read_skill({ name: "helix-vehicles", reference: "source-beamng" }).

reference.description: A reference file stem listed in the skill (no extension, no path).

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: List the available multiplayer world TEMPLATES — complete, publish-shaped worked worlds, one per capability cluster (presence, server/owned/shared/physics entities, collections, state machine, time, checkpoints, teams, voice channels). After get_started({kind:"multiplayer"}), pick the closest and read it with read_template({name}).

tools.name: read_template
tools.description: Read a complete, publish-shaped multiplayer world template: its DSL checklist, the full public/helix.json (incl. the multiplayer block), the client src/main.ts delta, and build/publish steps. Pick the name from the hub (get_started multiplayer) or list_templates — e.g. "hangout".

tools.name: create_device
tools.description: RETURNS A COMMAND, NOT DATA. This tool hands you a `helix …` command string to RUN yourself — it executes nothing and returns no results. The answer is in that command’s output. The only Device authoring entrypoint. Prepares the Creator CLI command that wraps an existing GLB in a declarative `helix.device/1` project. Devices are MCP/CLI-authored; there is intentionally no website workbench. After running it, edit the generated device.json through normal agent file tools, then call validate_device and test_device.

directory.description: Absolute path for the new Device project

model.description: Absolute path to the source GLB

template.description: Starting behavior/state contract. Television includes a permissioned Screen/App, universal text input, audio playback, and typed power/volume/audio ports.

tools.name: validate_device
tools.description: RETURNS A COMMAND, NOT DATA. This tool hands you a `helix …` command string to RUN yourself — it executes nothing and returns no results. The answer is in that command’s output. Prepare the Creator CLI validation command for a Device project. It fails closed on malformed definitions, invalid GLB bytes, missing named-node bindings, invalid typed state or Universal Action Surface controls, undeclared capabilities, and missing Home/World compatibility.

directory.description: Absolute Device project directory or device.json path

tools.name: test_device
tools.description: RETURNS A COMMAND, NOT DATA. This tool hands you a `helix …` command string to RUN yourself — it executes nothing and returns no results. The answer is in that command’s output. Prepare the Creator CLI Device simulation command. Use mode=both before publication: the exact same self-contained Device definition is exercised as an owned Item Instance and as a World-owned package instance; single covers every control/graph path and durable remount, multiplayer uses two independent clients against one authority state and refuses divergence.

directory.description: Absolute Device project directory or device.json path

tools.name: scaffold_world
tools.description: RETURNS A COMMAND, NOT DATA. This tool hands you a `helix …` command string to RUN yourself — it executes nothing and returns no results. The answer is in that command’s output. REQUIRED FIRST BUILD STEP — the command is `helix init <dir>`, and running it writes a complete, build-ready world project: package.json, vite.config.ts (base: "./"), tsconfig.json, index.html with the import-map markers + loading overlay, .gitignore, public/helix.json (v0.2, pinning humanoid-character AND engine-core), src/helix.runtime.ts, src/loading.ts, and a RUNNABLE src/main.ts — a real character world that builds and renders, with the world-owned InputService pre-wired (register game keys on it — never raw addEventListener), the floor collider, the world.ready() inspect hook, and the ability base resolved against document.baseURI so it survives the sub-path a published world is served from. DO NOT HAND-WRITE THESE FILES from the recipe prose: the recipe is explanation, the scaffold is the source. An agent that typed them out instead got four API calls wrong against the installed .d.ts and shipped a world that built, validated, and rendered nothing. Multiplayer scaffolds include proximity VOICE CHAT by default (the voice.proximity permission + the fail-soft join) — remove both only for a deliberately silent world. A scene scaffold can also come with GROUND: terrain: "<preset>" adds `--terrain <preset>`, which generates a 4 x 4-tile (1 km x 1 km) heightfield into public/scene/mall/terrain/, paints it from the preset, lifts the starter mall onto the flat spawn plateau, and declares it in the sealed document — public/.helixignore already covers terrain/, so those bytes stay a dev override. Scene worlds ONLY; read_doc({name:"terrain"}). Existing files are SKIPPED (safe to run inside an existing project); the CLI never destructively overwrites. Then: npm install → install_world_packages → npm run build → validate_world → `helix verify-subpath dist` → publish_world.

directory.description: Absolute path of the project directory (created if missing; existing files are kept unless overwrite)

title.description: World title shown in the tab, loading screen, and catalog

slug.description: URL-safe world slug (also the npm package name)

kind.description: character = single-player character world; multiplayer = presence world (grow the multiplayer block per the hub/templates); scene = IN DEVELOPMENT, opt-in ONLY when the creator explicitly asks for a world whose environment is a streamed HELIX Scene v2 document (or names a Scene document / Scene Package to stream) — never for "a scene", "a bare scene" or "no character", which are the plain recipe of get_started({ kind: "scene" }) or a character/multiplayer world with your own geometry. It is a multiplayer world whose ENVIRONMENT the scene system streams and the visual runtime lights — the scaffold seals a starter document into public/scene/, pins it in helix.json, and writes NO floor, props or lights, because the document carries geometry, materials, lights, spawn and collision

maxPlayers.description: multiplayer and scene worlds only; default 8. Keep modest — the platform clamps per-room

terrain.description: scene worlds ONLY: generate a 1 km x 1 km starter terrain from a built-in preset (meadow = gentle rolling grass, alpine = high massifs and snow, desert = dunes and mesas, coast = a shoreline that climbs inland, forest = wooded ridges and glens, volcanic = a crater cone in basalt). Omit for the flat starter scene

overwrite.description: Replace existing files (default false: skip them — the into-existing-project mode)

tools.name: terrain_generate
tools.description: Generate the GROUND a scene world stands on: runs `helix terrain generate` and writes a terrain source folder (per-tile 16-bit heights, the painted splats, terrain.json). Deterministic — the same preset, seed and size always produce the same bytes, so a re-run is free and a diff is real. USE IT for open ground under a scene world: a scene document declares the folder (the `terrain` element of a scene-elements document, or scaffold_world({ kind: "scene", terrain }) which already wired one) and the scene system streams the tiles as the world loads. A tile is 256 cells and this generator always writes the 1 m authoring grid, so a tile is 256 m: the default 4x4 grid is 1 km x 1 km (~2.4 MiB) and the cap is 16x16 = 4 km x 4 km (~39 MiB, ~25 s of work). A coarser authoring grid (0.5, 2, 4 or 8 m per sample) is an IMPORT-side choice — terrain_import takes outputMetresPerSample, generate has no spacing flag. Pass tiles OR sizeKm, never both. The preset picks BOTH the landform and the surfaces painted onto it. ALWAYS run terrain_inspect on the folder before publishing — folded layers and over-cap tiles are reported there and nowhere else. Terrain worlds run DYNAMIC lighting: never bake_world_lighting a world whose ground is streamed terrain. Full recipe: read_doc({ name: "terrain" }).

out.description: Absolute path of the terrain source folder to write (for a scaffolded scene world: public/scene/<folder>/terrain)

preset.description: Built-in preset: meadow (gentle rolling grass), alpine (massifs, snow above the treeline), desert (dunes and mesas), coast (a shoreline climbing inland), forest (wooded ridges and glens), volcanic (a crater cone in basalt)

seed.description: Landform seed; default 1. Change it for a different world of the same character

tiles.description: Grid size in tiles, e.g. "8x8". A tile is 256 cells — 256 m at 1 m per sample, 1 km at 4 m. Default 4x4 (1 km x 1 km at 1 m); the cap is 16x16

sizeKm.description: Square extent in kilometres instead of tiles, rounded to whole 256 m tiles (1 km = 4x4)

seaLevel.description: Flood the landform to this height in metres — everything below becomes water-level ground

holes.description: Absolute path to a greyscale PNG mask; pixels above mid-grey become holes in the ground (the hole is visual only — the collider under it stays solid, so do not use it for a pit the player falls through)

tools.name: terrain_import
tools.description: Turn an EXISTING heightmap — a real-world DEM, a sculpted export, ground shaped in another tool — into a terrain source folder: runs `helix terrain import`, resamples the file onto the authoring grid and paints it with a preset. Use it instead of terrain_generate whenever the shape of the ground is already decided somewhere else; everything after this point (inspect, the scene document, publishing, lighting) is identical. TWO SPACINGS, never confuse them: metresPerSample is the SOURCE posting — metres between two samples IN THE FILE, taken from the source data and never guessed — while outputMetresPerSample is the AUTHORING grid the world is built on, one of 0.5, 1, 2, 4 or 8 m (default 1). Author at 1 m for hand-scale ground a player walks over; go coarser when the extent is the point — a tile is 257 samples, so at 4 m one tile spans 1 km and a city-scale landscape costs a sixteenth of the tiles the same ground would at 1 m. HEIGHTS: png16 and r16 store 0..65535, so heightRange says what the darkest and brightest sample mean in metres (e.g. [0, 900]) and a wrong pair yields a plausible-looking world at the wrong scale; f32 (headerless little-endian float32) already holds absolute metres and REJECTS heightRange. Either way the ground belongs near y = 0 — the sky, the height fog and the numeric precision are all built for it, and the absolute altitude is a fact for the docs, not for the world: with png16/r16 shift heightRange (a 1900..3900 m DEM becomes [0, 2000]), with f32 pass heightOffset, which is added to every decoded height, so a DEM whose sea level reads 507 m re-bases with heightOffset: -507. The extension picks the format when format is omitted (.png, .r16/.raw, .f32). A source posting coarser than the authoring grid is upsampled with a cubic that keeps the slope continuous across the source samples; bilinear (resample) creases along every source row and column and the light draws each one. Three more inputs when the source needs them: origin puts sample (0, 0) at a chosen world position instead of centring the grid, samples gives the row length of a raw r16/f32 file that is not square, and splat + splatRoles paint from an AUTHORED RGBA image covering the grid extent — every role bound to a channel there takes its weight from that channel instead of the preset rule, and the roles left unnamed keep theirs. Then run terrain_inspect. read_doc({ name: "terrain" }).

file.description: Absolute path to the heightmap: a 16-bit PNG, a raw R16, or a headerless float32 (.f32) holding absolute metres

out.description: Absolute path of the terrain source folder to write

preset.description: Built-in preset id (meadow, alpine, desert, coast, forest, volcanic) to paint it with, or an ABSOLUTE path to a preset JSON file

metresPerSample.description: The SOURCE's ground resolution: metres between two samples IN THE FILE (a 30 m SRTM tile is 30). The grid the world is authored on is outputMetresPerSample

heightRange.description: [MIN, MAX] in metres that the darkest and brightest sample stand for, e.g. [0, 900] — shifted so the lowest ground sits near 0. REQUIRED for png16 and r16; REJECTED for f32, which already holds metres (re-base that one with heightOffset)

outputMetresPerSample.description: Metres between two samples of the AUTHORING grid: 0.5, 1, 2, 4 or 8, default 1. A tile is 257 samples, so it spans 256 m at 1 m and 1 km at 4 m — stay at 1 m for ground the player walks over, go coarse for a landscape whose extent is the point

heightOffset.description: Metres added to every decoded height: how an absolute-metres DEM is re-based so its sea level or its floor lands on 0 (a source whose sea level reads 507 m takes -507)

origin.description: [X, Z] world metres of sample (0, 0). Omitted, the grid is centred on the world origin

samples.description: Samples per row of a raw r16 or f32 file — a number, or "WxH" — needed only when its byte length is not a square. Ignored for png16

tiles.description: Grid size in tiles, e.g. "8x8". A tile is 256 cells — 256 m at 1 m per sample, 1 km at 4 m. Default 4x4 (1 km x 1 km at 1 m); the cap is 16x16

format.description: Override the format the file extension implies. f32 is headerless little-endian float32 in absolute metres

resample.description: How a coarser source posting reaches the authoring grid. Default cubic (slope-continuous across the source samples); bilinear creases at every source sample

splat.description: Absolute path to an AUTHORED RGBA8 PNG covering the grid extent; each channel bound by splatRoles replaces the preset rule for that role. Goes with splatRoles

splatRoles.description: Which role each splat channel carries, e.g. "R=base,G=low,B=slope". Roles: base, slope, peak, low, cavity, accent — the ones left unnamed keep their preset rules. Goes with splat

tools.name: terrain_inspect
tools.description: Report what a terrain source folder would actually ship, as numbers (`helix terrain inspect`): extent and tile count, authored samples, delivered bytes split into heights and splats, the height range, the coarse layer, which material roles the bake had to FOLD into a kept role on which tiles (a tile carries four layers; a preset may declare six), and every warning — an over-cap tile, an unbaked or splat-less folder, a grid past 16 x 16. THE GATE BEFORE PUBLISHING: none of this is visible in a screenshot and none of it is reported at publish time, so an unbaked or over-cap terrain otherwise ships silently. Read-only — it writes nothing. Returns the human summary followed by the same report as JSON.

dir.description: Absolute path of the terrain source folder (it holds terrain.json)

tools.name: placements_bake
tools.description: Bake deterministic instanced placements on authored terrain from a helix.placements-source/1 JSON file: solid records placed exactly, decorative records scattered by rule. The CLI validates prepared prototype LOD/texture closure, masks and stable solid placements, then writes placements.json and pinned binary regions. Local authoring only; this does not publish. Read the terrain recipe first.

source.description: Absolute path to placements source JSON

tools.name: placements_inspect
tools.description: Validate a baked placements folder and report prototype LODs, texture families, stable solid counts, region bytes and format caps. Read-only. Run after every bake and before scene publication; inspect runtime residency and visual passes as well.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Check HELIX login state. Publishing requires a logged-in creator account; if not logged in, drive the browser sign-in with start_login (the human completes it on the website).

tools.name: start_login
tools.description: Begin the HELIX browser sign-in for the helix3 environment (https://new.helixgame.com): opens the human's browser to the sign-in page and returns the URL — relay it if the browser did not open. The human completes the sign-in on the website; the minted token is captured and saved locally by this process (never returned to you). Poll check_login for the outcome. No-ops when already logged in to this environment.

openBrowser.description: Open the human's browser automatically (default true); false = only return the URL to relay

force.description: Sign in again even when already logged in to this environment (switch accounts)

tools.name: check_login
tools.description: Check the outcome of a start_login flow: pending (the human is still signing in — wait and re-check), done (logged in; credentials saved), or failed (timeout/denied — start_login again to retry).

tools.name: validate_world
tools.description: Validate a built world bundle directory (the Vite dist/ folder containing helix.json) against the exact rules the platform enforces at publish. Run this after building and fix every reported problem before publishing. A World whose engine systems are pinned to an exact version (not a ^ range) is refused: use ranges, and promote an engine fix instead of pinning to it.

directory.description: Absolute path to the built bundle directory (e.g. the dist/ folder)

tools.name: publish_world
tools.description: Publish a validated world bundle to HELIX Instant. Refuses a World whose engine systems are pinned to an exact version (use ^ ranges; there is no agent override — only the human can run the CLI with --allow-exact-engine-pin "<reason>"). Automatically captures a ready world thumbnail unless a custom cover is already selected, uploads it with the files, and activates the Build and cover together; returns the public play URL. Capture failure refuses publication. Requires login (check whoami first). Re-publishing the same slug creates the next build of that world.

directory.description: Absolute path to the built bundle directory (e.g. the dist/ folder)

thumbnail.description: Selected cover image path. Preserves an existing custom cover; otherwise uses this image, thumbnail.<ext> from the bundle, or automatically captures the ready world.

uploadSource.description: Opt in to uploading this world's source alongside the build so it can later be opened and edited in HELIX's website editor. Defaults to false — source is NEVER uploaded unless you set this, and it is the human's decision, not yours: ASK before setting it, because it sends their code to HELIX and some creators deliberately do not want that. The upload excludes node_modules, .git, dist and .vite, and anything the project's .gitignore excludes. It travels on a separate PRIVATE channel, not as part of the public build, and it does not change the published bundle in any way. Without it the world still publishes and plays exactly the same; it simply cannot be edited on the website afterwards, because nothing but the built bundle was ever sent.

sourceDir.description: Absolute path of the PROJECT directory to archive when uploadSource is true. Defaults to the parent of `directory`, which is right for the usual layout (publish dist/, source lives one level up). Set it only when the project root is somewhere else. Meaningless without uploadSource — passing it alone is refused rather than silently ignored.

tools.name: publish_unreal_world
tools.description: Publish a COOKED UNREAL world to HELIX and make it the world's active build. Takes the candidate directory the Unreal HelixWorldPublish commandlet writes (it contains world-build-manifest.json, its .sha256 receipt, cook-plan.json, and artifacts/<role>/…) — NOT an Unreal project directory, and NOT a web bundle. Verifies the candidate against the bytes on disk, registers the Build, uploads every artifact, has the server re-verify and countersign it, then promotes it. This is the ONLY way a cooked Unreal world reaches HELIX. Requires login (check whoami first) and the world must already exist (create_world). YOU CANNOT COOK FROM HERE: cooking is an Unreal Editor / commandlet step on a Windows machine with UE 5.8 — if there is no candidate directory yet, say so and stop rather than looking for one to invent. Web worlds use publish_world instead; the two are not interchangeable.

candidate.description: Absolute path to the cook output directory — the one containing world-build-manifest.json. Passing an Unreal project root or a web bundle is refused with the reason.

world.description: The HELIX world to publish to: its slug, or its UUID. The world must already exist — create_world mints one.

maxPlayers.description: Players per instance for the entry activity (1-1000). Ask the human if the world does not imply one.

activityId.description: Activity id for the entry map. Defaults to 'default'; only set it for a world with several named activities.

visibility.description: Catalog visibility to set when the build is promoted. Omit to leave the world's current visibility alone. Going 'public' lists it for everyone — that is the human's call, not yours.

promote.description: Defaults to true: the uploaded build becomes the active release. Set false to upload and verify WITHOUT changing what players get — use this to stage a build for review.

verifyDelivery.description: After promoting, re-read what a client would actually download and check it matches what was uploaded. Cheap; worth it on a first publish.

tools.name: unreal_doctor
tools.description: Diagnose a HELIX Unreal (UE 5.8) project for World publishing. Two layers, same implementations the human CLI uses: a static publish-readiness validation (helix.unreal.json + project shape, no editor needed), and optionally the SDK’s in-editor Project Doctor commandlet (engine=true; needs UE_ROOT on this machine) which can also APPLY every automatable fix (fix=true — previewed, surgical, guesses are skipped with reasons). Findings come back machine-readable with a who-must-act verdict: pass / fixable / creator-action / unsupported.

project.description: project directory holding the .uproject (or the .uproject path for the static layer)

engine.description: also run the in-editor SDK Doctor commandlet (requires UE_ROOT)

fix.description: apply automatable in-editor fixes, then re-scan (implies engine)

tools.name: inspect_world
tools.description: Measure the layout of a built world as DATA (same code path as `helix world inspect`): boots it headlessly, snapshots the scene graph — world positions, extents, oriented boxes, visibility, physics colliders — and runs placement checks: floating/sunk/intersecting geometry, collider-vs-visual divergence (including the classic half-extent/full-size slip), mirrored or degenerate transforms, stray coordinates. THE INNER LOOP FOR PLACEMENT: measure here until the numbers are right (this answers "is the bench 0.4 m in the air" exactly — a screenshot measurably cannot), then capture_world_screenshot ONCE before handing to a human. FINDINGS ARE MEASUREMENTS, NOT VERDICTS: check each against your intent. Hovering pickups, ramps embedded in the ground, and walls overlapping at their corners all warn on perfectly good worlds — a warn that matches what you meant needs no fix; a warn that surprises you is the bug. NEVER edit geometry just to silence a finding. WHAT IT CANNOT ANSWER: whether the scene READS as intended — materials, lighting mood, animation, art direction — that is the closing screenshot check. Requires the world to integrate @helix/engine-core/inspect (one line at end of boot: world.ready({ scene, body, spawn }) — read_doc "world-inspect"; the scaffold recipe shows the wiring). EXISTING worlds scaffolded before this integration usually lack the call — check_for_updates({ projectDir }) reports the wiring state up front, cheaper than a 60s timeout. DENSE HAND-BUILT worlds warn a lot on intended decor (hanging lights read as floating): uniform same-parent runs collapse to one line automatically, and after you adjudicate, writeBaseline persists the verdict so later inspects report only what CHANGED. Object paths are canonicalized (content order) — stable across runs; coordinates remain the strongest cross-run handle.

directory.description: Absolute path to the built world bundle directory (same dir publish_world takes)

report.description: Report sections (default ["anomalies"]). "roster" = the grouped object inventory with sizes/positions; "colliders" = the physics roster; "zones" = the declared multiplayer.json trigger volumes with their rest surfaces and touched geometry. Ask for what you need — a large world renders long.

json.description: Return the raw { snapshot, analysis } JSON instead of the rendered report — for programmatic follow-up on exact numbers. CAUTION on large worlds: the raw snapshot is ~350 bytes PER OBJECT (a 5000-object world is ~2 MB) — prefer the rendered report (grouped roster, per-rule capped findings) and request json only when you need every number.

focusNear.description: THE SINGLE-OBJECT LENS: report only the object(s) near this world-space point — the fastest way to check the thing you just placed, because YOU wrote its coordinates. Returns exact position, size, AABB, FACING (yaw + world direction, with TOWARD / AWAY from / side-on relations to nearby objects — how you catch the chair pointing away from its table), touching colliders, and only the findings involving it. Analysis still runs whole-world; this scopes the report. No naming needed.

focus.description: Alternative lens: report only objects whose path contains this substring (case-insensitive) — for named objects and imported GLB assets, whose node names survive export.

settleMs.description: Settle time between world-ready and the snapshot (default 750 ms). Raise it for worlds whose props animate into place.

browser.description: Diagnostic override: force this one launch candidate, no fallback. The default chain (bundled Chromium, then system Chrome, then system Edge) is normally correct.

writeBaseline.description: Accept ALL current findings into inspect.baseline.json beside the world project — after that, inspect reports only what CHANGED (new findings, plus accepted ones that no longer occur). Use AFTER adjudicating the findings against intent (the hanging decor is meant to hang), and tell the user you wrote it. Entries key on rule + world-space anchor, so they survive rebuilds and renumbering.

showAccepted.description: Render baseline-accepted findings too instead of hiding them behind the baseline summary line.

tools.name: world_metrics
tools.description: The static traversal/movement reference from a world’s OWN installed character system — read it instead of guessing spatial constraints while building: player capsule (height/radius/crouch), step height (what auto-steps vs blocks), max walkable slope, movement speeds, and the derived jump envelope (air time, max flat-ground gap at run/sprint) plus corridor/ceiling clearances. Values are the system DEFAULTS a world starts from; worlds may override via config. Use it to size gaps, steps, ramps, corridors, and ceilings BEFORE placing geometry, and pair it with inspect_world to verify what you placed.

projectDir.description: Absolute path to the world project (the dir with helix.json — must be npm-installed + install_world_packages'd so its pinned system is present)

tools.name: analyze_scene_performance
tools.description: EXECUTES the Creator CLI scene performance analyzer and returns its report to the agent. Call after the first build or imported Scene exists, then again with final snapshot/Package/runtime evidence. It runs canonical Scene/Package validation, and unresolved non-bundle resources keep affected checks unknown. It separates authored mesh-definition triangles from runtime submitted triangles; file-local/slot/unique/source/native/Package/observed Palette materials; declared/GPU texture costs; owned/transitive/cold/warm delivery; and static estimated reference-budget utilization from supplied runtime claims. Runtime proof records compile/stream/GI readiness, grounded route, occupancy, frame count/duration, bundle/dirty-code identity, canvas/DPR, and internal compositor resolution separately. Unknown metrics stay unknown and never improve the result. Read scene-performance for the interpretation and matched visual-QA workflow.

directory.description: Absolute directory containing the built bundle or Scene-owned resources

scene.description: Exact Scene v2 JSON; supplies authoritative resource roles/integrity, surfaces, and stream groups

package.description: Exact Continuum Package version JSON; supplies semantic material bindings/dependencies and transitive closure

snapshot.description: inspect_world snapshot JSON for visible-scene triangles

perf.description: Runtime receipt. The report treats its values as supplied claims and reports byte/identity binding separately.

profile.description: Existing Palette Showcase reference profile; default web-desktop-balanced. It is a comparison reference, not a universal Scene guarantee.

tools.name: capture_world_screenshot
tools.description: Capture headless screenshots of a built world via its in-page screenshot helper (Playwright, in-process — same code path as the `helix screenshot` CLI command). Returns a compact preview image per capture PLUS a text block listing every file written. LOOK at the returned image(s) and judge the framing before attaching one with set_world_thumbnail. FOR PLACEMENT QUESTIONS USE inspect_world, NOT this tool — do not answer "is it floating / how far apart / does it fit" by looking harder; distances and depth read from an image are measurably unreliable. This is the CLOSING check for how the scene reads (framing, materials, lighting, mood), after the numbers are already right. Prefer a declared shot (world code calls screenshots.register — read_doc "screenshots") over the camera/lookAt/fov override or blindMs, both non-deterministic fallbacks.

directory.description: Absolute path to the world's built bundle directory (same dir publish_world takes)

shot.description: Capture only this declared shot (default: every declared shot)

camera.description: Override pose: camera position [x, y, z] — bypasses declared shots, writes custom.png

lookAt.description: Override pose: look-at point [x, y, z] (only applied together with camera)

fov.description: Override pose: field of view in degrees (only applied together with camera)

preview.description: Also capture each shot at 2560x1440 to <shot>.preview.png

blindMs.description: Explicit opt-in fallback for worlds WITHOUT the helper: skip the readiness wait, delay this many ms, then screenshot the canvas. Non-deterministic — a last resort, never a stable thumbnail source.

out.description: Output directory (default: a "screenshots" folder next to `directory`)

browser.description: Diagnostic override: force this one launch candidate, no fallback. The default chain (bundled Chromium, then system Chrome, then system Edge) is normally correct.

previewImages.description: How many downscaled preview image blocks to return (default 3). Pass 0 to skip image blocks entirely — right when capturing a gallery for the human rather than inspecting framing yourself; every written file path is always listed in the text block either way.

tools.name: inspect_npc
tools.description: MEASURE what a world's NPCs actually DO, as numbers (same code path as the CLI): boots the built world headlessly, watches it run for a few seconds, and reports per NPC — distance actually walked vs distance actually GAINED (the progress ratio: 1.00 is a straight line, 0.1 is a shuffle), closest approach and final distance to a target you name, STUCK WINDOWS using the driver's own rule (under 0.35 m of ground made in 1.5 s — the same stall its sideways commit fires on), the arrived edges with timestamps, how much of the run held a planned nav path at all, and the locomotion + world-state timelines. THIS IS THE INNER LOOP: measure here until the numbers are right, THEN capture_npc once to look. The order is a rule, not a preference — behaviour bugs on this system are SILENT and invisible in a still frame: an NPC that chases perfectly and never attacks (arrived read after the seek instead of before), one that grinds into a corner forever (re-seeking every frame, which disables the stuck commit), one on the default stand body that can never walk at all, and a NavGrid that degraded to direct steering without a word. Each of those has a signature in this report and none of them has one in a screenshot. REQUIRES the world to hand its NPC pool to the inspect helper — world.ready({ scene, body, spawn, npcs, npcState }) — and to have been REBUILT since; a world that is inspect-wired but passes no npcs fails here with the exact wiring line. read_doc({ name: "npc-world" }) has the recipe.

directory.description: Absolute path to the BUILT world bundle directory (the same dir inspect_world and publish_world take — usually <project>/dist, NOT the project root the gesture tools take)

seconds.description: How long to watch, in seconds (default 8). Long enough for the behaviour to complete a cycle: a chase that takes 12 s to cross the level reads as "never arrived" in a 4 s window.

sampleHz.description: Samples per second (default 10). 10 Hz resolves the 1.5 s stuck window and every state change worth naming; raise it only to time a fast edge.

npc.description: Report only this NPC id. Every id the world reported still appears in the roster line, so a typo is obvious rather than silent.

target.description: World-space point [x, y, z] the NPC is supposed to reach — adds start/closest/final distance and how much ground it CLOSED. This is the measurement that answers "is the chase actually working", which no position dump does.

settleMs.description: Settle time between world-ready and the first sample (default 750 ms). Raise it for worlds whose NPCs spawn behind an await.

browser.description: Diagnostic override: force this one launch candidate, no fallback. The default chain (bundled Chromium, then system Chrome, then system Edge) is normally correct.

json.description: Return the raw inspection JSON instead of the rendered report — every sample-derived number, for programmatic follow-up. The rendered report is the right default; it names what each number means.

tools.name: capture_npc
tools.description: LOOK at a world's NPCs: a filmstrip of the running world — a canvas frame at each of several moments — where every frame is CAPTIONED with the NPC sample taken at that same instant (position, locomotion state, arrived, nav path, your own world state). Returns preview images plus the full list of files and captions. THE CLOSING CHECK, NEVER THE FIRST CALL: run inspect_npc until the numbers are right, then capture once. A frame answers what measurement cannot — is the NPC actually there, is it wearing the right body, is it T-posing, is it standing inside the counter — and answers nothing about distance, progress or whether a chase is closing; take all of that from inspect_npc, which is why the caption rides along. NO CAMERA CONTROL: the inspect lane exposes no way to aim a camera at an NPC, so these are plain full-view frames of whatever the world itself is showing. If the NPC is off-screen in the world's own view, that is what you will get — frame the world's camera in world code, or read the numbers instead. Same requirement as inspect_npc: the world must pass npcs to world.ready(...) and have been rebuilt since.

directory.description: Absolute path to the BUILT world bundle directory (the same dir inspect_world and publish_world take — usually <project>/dist)

npc.description: Caption only this NPC id (the frames themselves are the whole view either way)

frames.description: How many frames across the window (default 6)

seconds.description: The window the frames are spread over, in seconds (default 6) — frames are evenly spaced across it

settleMs.description: Settle time between world-ready and the first frame (default 750 ms)

out.description: Directory to write the PNGs into (default: a fresh temp dir, whose path is reported)

browser.description: Diagnostic override: force this one launch candidate, no fallback.

previewImages.description: How many downscaled preview image blocks to return (default 3). Pass 0 to skip images entirely — every written file and its caption is listed in the text block either way.

tools.name: bake_world_lighting
tools.description: Bake a world's lighting field from its BUILT bundle and point its visual contract at the artifact (same code path as `helix bake-lighting`): serves the build headlessly, drives the in-page bake driver across sun keyframes plus the practical lights, audits and repairs the probe field, then writes helix.visuals.bake.json and patches helix.visuals.json to mode "baked" in BOTH the source public/ and the built root. USE IT FOR a bounded, static-geometry world whose visual contract declares — or should declare — mode "baked": interiors, arenas, dioramas, anything whose geometry and lights do not move. A BOUNDED INTERIOR authors probes: { center, size } in helix.visuals.json to fit the bake volume to its room BEFORE baking — the default volume is sized for open ground, and the bake warns when its volume does not fit the play space (heed that warning by authoring the block and re-baking); an authored center also pins the still-dynamic world's runtime volume to the same box, so author the block at build time, not bake time. Run it AFTER npm run build, on the built world, never on an unbuilt source tree, and expect MINUTES of blocking GPU work (a small world is a minute or two — do not interrupt it, and do not call it in a loop). NOTHING IT WRITES SHIPS until the world is re-validated and re-published: build → bake_world_lighting → validate_world → publish_world, and re-bake whenever the geometry, the lights, or any TRANSPORT knob in helix.visuals.json changes (sun, sky, environment, shadows, probes — the bake photographs all of them). LEAVE keys ALONE unless you know better: omitted, the engine plans them — ONE key for a static sun (timeOfDay.cycleSeconds 0), 9 for a cycle — and the pointer it writes records the count as bakedLighting.keys, which validate_world re-checks against the world clock. Pass gpu: true to bake on the machine GPU through a system Chrome/Edge when the wait hurts (measured 41 s against 27 minutes on a 45 MiB world); it is not bit-reproducible across machines, so the software renderer stays the default. It fails loudly rather than write a wrong artifact — an unbuilt world, a world that never publishes the bake handle (nothing called createVisualRuntime, so it is not runtime-lit and has no probe field), a boot slower than timeoutSeconds, or the donor-occlusion gate — and the failure text leads with the page errors, which are the diagnosis. It never installs a browser: a launch failure relays the install instructions for the human. The decision tree (baked vs dynamic vs the opt-out) and the full helix.visuals.json reference: read_doc({name:"lighting-world"}).

directory.description: Absolute path to the world project directory (its dist/ is baked and its public/ contract patched) or to the built bundle directory itself

keys.description: Sun keyframes to capture. OMITTED = the engine plans them: ONE for a static sun (timeOfDay.cycleSeconds 0 or absent), 9 for a cycle — which is what you want, so leave it out. A static world baked at 9 keys pays ~9x the artifact bytes for eight hours nobody plays, and keys: 1 on a CYCLING world is refused outright.

gpu.description: Bake on the machine GPU through a system Chrome/Edge instead of the bundled software renderer — measured 41 s against 27 minutes on a 45 MiB world. NOT bit-reproducible across machines, which is why software stays the default: use it while iterating, and remember the shipped artifact is whatever the last bake wrote.

timeoutSeconds.description: Boot budget in seconds — the wait for the bake handle, NOT a cap on the bake itself. Omitted, the bake scales it with the bundle size (20 s per MiB, floor 300 s), which is normally right; raise it when the headless boot is slow for some OTHER reason. A world that never publishes the handle fails with that diagnosis instead.

tools.name: inspect_gesture
tools.description: MEASURE a pose-DSL gesture clip without a browser (same code path as `helix gesture inspect`). Runs the world's OWN installed character system, so what it reports is what the world renders. Use it after writing or editing ANY gesture clip, BEFORE asking a human to look: it is the only way to tell a good pose from a broken one without eyes. Reports (a) compile errors and natural-range warnings, (b) per-bone landmark readback in plain English at any time ("hand_r: at head height, 0.34m to the character-right, palm faces forward"), (c) with motion:true, what the clip DOES over time — extent per axis, dominant direction, purity, reversals, (d) with axes:true, what a +10° edit to each keyed axis actually does AT THE POSED CHAIN, which the rest-frame axis table cannot tell you once a parent has rotated, (e) for clips with compile-time ik keys, the ik-goals report: target vs actual landing (cm error) + the resolved joint eulers — a clip using ik on a world whose installed system predates IK (added in 0.2.15) fails with a version message; fix via install_world_packages. Needs a world that has been npm-installed and install_world_packages'd.

clip.description: Absolute path to the gesture clip .json file

world.description: Absolute path to the world project directory (the one holding public/helix_modules — NOT dist/)

t.description: Readback times: seconds (0.35) or percentages of duration ("50%"). Default [0] — pass the moments that matter, e.g. the peak of the pose.

bones.description: Bones to report (default clavicle_r, upperarm_r, lowerarm_r, hand_r, head, spine_03). hand_l/hand_r additionally report palm + finger facing, self-calibrated from the rig.

motion.description: Report what the clip does over time. Pair with motionWindow — otherwise the rest→pose→rest travel dominates every number and hides the gesture.

motionWindow.description: Restrict motion analysis to t=[a,b] — the sustained part of the clip

axes.description: Report what a +10° edit to each keyed axis does at the posed chain — use this when a value that "should" work does not

probe.description: Which bone axes measures the effect on (default: the last bones entry that exists)

rig.description: Measure against a custom character GLB instead of the canonical helix-humanoid skeleton (conform aims bones at each character's own joints, so extremity frames differ by up to ~20°)

attach.description: Absolute path to a prop .glb to measure attached to the pose. Adds (e): the prop bbox in the grip-socket frame ("0.06m behind the grip point"), a unit verdict (the runtime rejects props spanning over 2 m), and where the prop lands at each t. Measure here FIRST; capture_gesture with the same attach params is the closing look.

attachSocket.description: Socket to attach to (default: the preset's, then hand_r.grip). Grip sockets are semantic held-item frames: +z = where the item points, +y = the item's up — a prop authored grip-at-origin, +z out, +y up, in meters needs no offsets.

attachPreset.description: Held-item category (pistol, rifle, sword, mug, flashlight, torch, phone) contributing default socket + offsets

attachOffset.description: Socket-local position offset in meters (XYZ) — overrides the preset

attachRotation.description: Socket-local rotation in degrees (XYZ) — overrides the preset

tools.name: capture_gesture
tools.description: LOOK at a pose-DSL gesture: renders the clip as a contact sheet — front and side, evenly spaced across the clip — and returns it as an image. This is the CLOSING check, not the inner loop: measure with inspect_gesture until the numbers are right (it is milliseconds), then capture once before handing the clip to a human, because "how it reads" is the one thing measurement cannot tell you. DO NOT CALL THIS FIRST — a clip that still has compile warnings is not ready to look at, and the render cannot tell you what those warnings would have. Each call costs a headless browser launch, a few seconds. Always renders the DEFAULT character: a clip replicates by NAME and plays on whatever body each player has, so a pose is authored against the canonical body every custom character is conformed to — the sheet is a reference render, not a preview of any particular player's view. Needs a world that has been npm-installed and install_world_packages'd. WHAT THE IMAGE CAN AND CANNOT ANSWER: trust it for silhouette, which limb is where, joint bend direction and gross orientation — the 'does this read as a person doing X' judgement no measurement can make. Do NOT read distances or which body part moved off it. That is measurably unreliable: an elbow sitting 0.20m FORWARD was read as 'tucked against the ribs', and a wind-up where the TORSO had leaned 0.19m back was read as 'the arms are behind the head'. Depth magnitude is the weak axis and the three-quarter view does not fix it — it fixes in-front-versus-behind ORDERING only. Natural-range violations are invisible in a render entirely. So when the image raises a question, answer it with inspect_gesture, never by looking harder.

clip.description: Absolute path to the gesture clip .json file

world.description: Absolute path to the world project directory (the one holding public/helix_modules — NOT dist/)

frames.description: How many evenly spaced sample times across the clip (default 5 — 0/25/50/75/100%)

views.description: Up to two camera angles. left/right are the CHARACTER's OWN sides, matching the readback's character-left/character-right — not the viewer's; three-quarter is 40 degrees off the front, on the side the clip uses. YOU RARELY NEED THIS: the default is chosen per mode — a time sequence gets front + the side the clip actually keys (derived from its bones and mask), which is the ORTHOGONAL pair that makes 'moves side-to-side, not front-to-back' readable; a single moment (at) gets front + three-quarter, which lifts a limb clear of the torso instead of hiding it behind. Override for a reach behind the body. Do not pair front with back, or left with right: each looks down ONE axis, so neither view shows depth.

at.description: Capture ONE moment instead of a sequence — seconds (0.6) or a percentage ('60%'). The two views then sit SIDE BY SIDE at roughly 1.8x the size, which is what you want when a human asks you to fix one specific thing: the whole image budget goes to that instant instead of a fifth of it. Omit for the time sequence.

out.description: Where to write the PNG (default: alongside the clip as <clip>.sheet.png)

attach.description: Absolute path to a prop .glb to render attached while the clip plays. MEASURE BEFORE PIXELS: converge the numbers with inspect_gesture and the same attach params first — the render shows how the held prop reads, not where it is.

attachSocket.description: Socket to attach to (default: the preset's, then hand_r.grip)

attachPreset.description: Held-item category (pistol, rifle, sword, mug, flashlight, torch, phone) contributing default socket + offsets

attachOffset.description: Socket-local position offset in meters (XYZ) — overrides the preset

attachRotation.description: Socket-local rotation in degrees (XYZ) — overrides the preset

tools.name: gesture_axis_table
tools.description: The bone axis reference for authoring pose-DSL gestures: per bone group, what each Euler axis DOES in human terms, plus the advisory natural range per axis (outside it the compiler warns, it does not fail). Call this BEFORE picking rotation values — guessing costs a revise cycle per bone. Read live from the humanoid-character version THIS world pinned, which is why it takes a world dir and why no doc reproduces the table. Meanings hold FROM REST ONLY: rotations chain, so once a parent has rotated use inspect_gesture with axes:true instead — or state a hand-position goal as a compile-time ik key (≥ 0.2.15) and skip joint-space search entirely.

world.description: Absolute path to the world project directory (the one holding public/helix_modules — NOT dist/)

tools.name: set_world_thumbnail
tools.description: RETURNS A COMMAND, NOT DATA. This tool hands you a `helix …` command string to RUN yourself — it executes nothing and returns no results. The answer is in that command’s output. Attach a custom thumbnail or preview image to a published world (fills the generated-placeholder slot). Filling an EMPTY slot is a normal finishing step after a good capture — do it without asking. Pass overwrite ONLY when the human explicitly asked to replace an existing image; an occupied slot without overwrite is refused by the CLI (with the current URL intact) so you can relay the situation instead of silently skipping it.

file.description: Absolute path to a local image file (png, jpg/jpeg, or webp)

kind.description: Media slot to fill: thumbnail (cover everywhere, 1280x720) or preview (one extra detail-carousel slide, 2560x1440). Default thumbnail.

overwrite.description: Replace an already-set slot — only on an explicit human request, never automatically

tools.name: clear_world_thumbnail
tools.description: RETURNS A COMMAND, NOT DATA. This tool hands you a `helix …` command string to RUN yourself — it executes nothing and returns no results. The answer is in that command’s output. Revert a world thumbnail/preview slot to the auto-generated placeholder.

kind.description: Media slot to clear: thumbnail or preview. Default thumbnail.

tools.name: set_preview_video
tools.description: RETURNS A COMMAND, NOT DATA. This tool hands you a `helix …` command string to RUN yourself — it executes nothing and returns no results. The answer is in that command’s output. Set or clear a published world's YouTube preview. The CLI and the API own what counts as a valid YouTube link — the URL is normalised server-side.

tools.name: list_cosmetic_slots
tools.description: RETURNS A COMMAND, NOT DATA. This tool hands you a `helix …` command string to RUN yourself — it executes nothing and returns no results. The answer is in that command’s output. Print the Character-Creator cosmetic slot and gender vocabulary through the HELIX creator CLI.

tools.name: validate_vehicle
tools.description: Run the HELIX vehicle validator (executes the bundled `helix vehicle validate`) on a vehicle package (helix.vehicle-package/2) and, with glb, its model — BEFORE any publish — and return its report and exit code. It checks the engine's own package validator (a package with an error never spawns, and publish does not catch it), the publish gate (distributable provenance, wheelVisuals, required fields), groundToBodyOrigin = wheelRadius + staticRideHeight (locked after first publish), the GLB host manifest in asset.extras.HELIX_vehicle (without it the car is no add-on host), the host-frame bind nodes (a car offering a boot/bonnet socket needs the lid's mount node and a vehicle_root node owning it, or a bound add-on throws in the runtime and the car is never presented: HOST_BIND_*), all four wheel nodes with their origins AT THE HUB, frame orientation, the platform budgets (24 draws, 90k triangles, 48 materials, 2048 px), articulation panel nodes and their controls, the specialty componentBuild digest (prints the computed value), and the drive figures against `targets` (simulate_vehicle; skip with noSimulate). Exit 0 = no errors. It also prints, as warnings, SPEED_LIMITER_IS_A_MARKET_GOVERNOR, TORQUE_CURVE_EXCEEDS_DECLARED_CRANK_FIGURES and AWD_DRIVE_BIAS_* (the platform car runs ungoverned on the maker's declared crank figures; physics-from-specs). With cabin: true it also runs check_vehicle_cabin's per-seat fit (errors CABIN_CHECK_FAIL, warnings CABIN_CHECK_WARN); a car that declares more than two seats is pointed at it. read_doc({name:"vehicles"}) is the contract it enforces.

vehiclePackage.description: Absolute path to the vehicle package JSON.

glb.description: Absolute path to the vehicle GLB to check against the package. Always pass it before a publish.

noSimulate.description: Skip the drive-figure check against targets (structure only).

offline.description: Drive with the last cached engine runtime; never fetch it.

cabin.description: Also run the offline cabin check (every declared seat; FAIL rows are errors). Needs glb.

tools.name: simulate_vehicle
tools.description: Drive an UNPUBLISHED vehicle package offline on the platform's own vehicle runtime (executes the bundled `helix vehicle simulate`; it fetches and caches the live humanoid-character runtime) and return 0–100 km/h, 0–60 mph, quarter mile, top speed, ungoverned top speed, 100–0 km/h and 60–0 mph braking, skidpad lateral g, turbo lag, the gears used and the rest pose (grounded, pitch and roll ≤ 3°), each compared with the package's `targets` (a row passes when |simulated − target| / target ≤ its tolerance fraction). KEYBOARD LAUNCH: it also launches the car the way a keyboard player does (W 0→1 in one tick, A/D taps with 100 ms reactions holding a lane; W+A/D is normalised to 0.707 throttle; a land-v2 car has traction control only when its package authors `simulation.land.tractionControl`, which this models exactly as live and reports on a `traction control:` line) and nudges the yaw 0.2 rad/s hands-off at 20/40/60/100 km/h and as each upshift re-engages: keyboard 0–100 vs the instrument, wheelspin per gear, post-shift yaw, lane offset. A nudge that grows into a spin FAILS "not drivable on a keyboard" (validate_vehicle reports it as the warning SIMULATED_KEYBOARD_LAUNCH_UNDRIVABLE; tune only with sourced levers, or author traction control (the real system, or a declared playability aid) — physics-from-specs "Drivable on a keyboard" and "Traction control"). Exit 0 = every compared figure passes and the keyboard launch does not FAIL; 1 = a figure is out of tolerance, the rest pose is wrong or the car is not drivable on a keyboard; 2 = could not simulate. validate_vehicle runs the same check. It also reports the SHIFT SCHEME: a gearbox with `auto.enabled` false cannot shift itself, so the figures cannot be reached and the live car will pin 1st gear unless the player uses the manual keys — and a manual-kind box with auto enabled is reported as "simulated with auto-shift; live manual-shift unverified". Run it after every physics edit and before the first mint: it is the only way to know a car is too quick or stops too short without publishing it. Only grip.peak and suspension.* (and, for a turbo car, the derated low end of the curve) are yours to tune toward the targets (read_skill helix-vehicles reference "physics-from-specs"). Also prints the engine-policy warnings SPEED_LIMITER_IS_A_MARKET_GOVERNOR (speedLimiterKph below 0.9 × the ungoverned top speed: the platform car runs ungoverned and the live solver never applies a limiter; null it and set targets.topSpeedKph to the ungoverned figure), TORQUE_CURVE_EXCEEDS_DECLARED_CRANK_FIGURES (a torque curve or peak field more than 5 % above the maker's declared crank figures: put losses in drivetrainEfficiency and drag, never inflate the curve) and AWD_DRIVE_BIAS_* (driveBiasFront must be strictly between 0 and 1 and equal centre.torqueSplit on an AWD car) — see physics-from-specs.

target.description: Absolute path to the vehicle package directory or its vehicle-package.json.

itemId.description: Simulate a PUBLISHED vehicle item's stored package instead (public read) — for example a control car such as the live 993.

spec.description: Absolute path to an extra target file to compare against: a package, { targets: {…} }, or a reference spec with perf.* figures (perf.0_100_kmh_s, perf.braking_100_0_m, …; a leaf is a number or { value, tol_pct }, default ±10 %).

offline.description: Use only the cached runtime; never fetch it.

noKeyboardLaunch.description: Skip the keyboard launch and its hands-off yaw probe (faster; only while iterating on figures).

tools.name: get_vehicle_reference_package
tools.description: Copy the reference vehicle package — the complete helix.vehicle-package/2 of the live Porsche 911 (993), which passes visual QA and drives live — to a path you name, and return a short summary of its blocks. It is about 75k characters of JSON, too large for any tool output, so it is never returned inline: read the copied file block by block. Its notes are stripped of the 993's own provenance; replace EVERY number, citation and slot note with your car's. Its AUDIO block is shape only: the 993's sounds are not your car's, so replace the whole block with your car's sound from its most accurate simulator mod (import_vehicle_audio, never synthesised) and give every slot its provenance. What to keep, change or delete: read_skill({ name: "helix-vehicles", reference: "reference-package" }).

out.description: Absolute path of the file to write (…/vehicle-package.json), or a directory to write reference-package.json into.

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file. Off by default, so your edited package is never clobbered.

tools.name: check_vehicle_host
tools.description: Read a published vehicle's add-on surface the way the customizer sees it (public reads, no sign-in): its slot board (host kind, measured sockets / nodes / tunable paths, hide grants) and every add-on that FITS it, grouped by slot type with price, against the required minimum parts set (wheels, exhaust, ECU, gearbox, suspension, brakes, anti-roll bars; spoiler where the real car has one). Also runs the web customizer's own add-on guard on EVERY fitting add-on's exact Package pin (the CLI's vendored copy of the customizer's meshless guard, public reads): a part the customizer would refuse to equip or save ("Add-on definition declares visual geometry but has no public web GLB.", a visual mount with no GLB, a wrong root) is named with the customizer's message. Also fails when the car's GLB lacks the nodes a host-frame add-on binds to (HOST_BIND_ROOT_MISSING: no vehicle_root node; HOST_BIND_MOUNT_NODE_MISSING: an offered boot/bonnet socket with no node; HOST_BIND_ROOT_NOT_OWNER: the lid is outside vehicle_root), and when any published add-on's bind root is absent from the car: the message names the node, the slot and the add-on and says to add an empty node of that name over the car's top-level nodes. Fails when the car is not a host (its GLB had no asset.extras.HELIX_vehicle at mint), when the board has no sockets or no tunable paths, when a required part is missing or not for sale, or when any fitting add-on would be refused by the customizer. Run it after the car is published and after each of its add-ons.

tools.name: publish_vehicle
tools.description: Publish a vehicle end to end from a package directory, Package-first (executes the bundled `helix vehicle publish`; minutes, not seconds) and return its output and exit code. Directory: vehicle-package.json, model.glb carrying asset.extras.HELIX_vehicle, the WAVs beside it or in audio/, and publish.json { title, description, tags, version, contentRating, provenance: { kind: "authored"|"imported"|"generated", source }, hostGrantExtensions: { "whl.wheel": { "hide": ["rim_*"] }, … } }. It validates (package, GLB, host manifest, the drive against targets, every audio sample and its provenance), REFUSES synthesised or generated audio (AUDIO_SYNTHESISED) a car without sourced engine audio (AUDIO_ENGINE_UNSOURCED — the engine's built-in synthesised fallback engine is not an engine sound for a published car; run import_vehicle_audio first) and any empty or default-falling-back slot (AUDIO_SLOT_UNSOURCED — every one of the 31 slots needs a sourced recording; platform defaults are never an answer), uploads the GLB and WAVs as public objects, builds the root (mesh.visual pinned to the uploaded GLB, audio rows pinned, the hide grants sealed in), seals a public `vehicle` Package, makes the Item from that exact Version, and reads everything back (pin, package identity, mesh, audio, the add-on host board). It opens no offer. With itemId + version + reason it seals a STAGED version into the same car's Package and moves the item (or stops at staged-awaiting-visual-qa on a listed car) — the only way to change a car that exists; never mint a second copy. ACTIVATE a new version of a LISTED car only by re-running this same call after visual QA passes (pin and properties.vehiclePackage move together); NEVER `helix item set-version` for a vehicle (it moves the pin but not properties.vehiclePackage, so the car keeps serving its old package). Resumable: re-run the same call after any failure (ledger in <dir>/.helix-publish). Exit 0 = published and verified (or staged awaiting visual QA); 1 = a check failed; 2 = could not run. Run dryRun first. Answers NOT AVAILABLE when the bundled CLI has no vehicle mint.

dir.description: Absolute path to the vehicle package directory.

title.description: Display title (default: publish.json title, then the package displayName).

glb.description: Absolute path to the drawn model when the directory holds more than one .glb.

itemId.description: Publish a new version of this existing vehicle item instead of minting one.

version.description: Package Version to seal (default 1.0.0; required with itemId).

reason.description: With itemId: why the version moves (1–500 chars).

noSimulate.description: Skip the drive check against targets.

dryRun.description: Validate, check audio (provenance and sourcing included) and run the seal-side validation (provenance.source <= 256 chars, contentRating, Package shape); nothing is uploaded or charged.

tools.name: preview_vehicle
tools.description: Render an UNPUBLISHED vehicle (a package directory, or vehicle-package.json + GLB, that exists only on disk) headless in the REAL HELIX runtime and measure it (executes the bundled `helix vehicle preview`; several minutes), before the first mint locks groundToBodyOrigin forever. Nothing is uploaded or recorded. Returns a per-wheel stance table and PASS/FAIL per check — ride height vs your declared groundToBodyOrigin (with the value to declare instead), wheels at hubs, arch clearance, spin, steering, panels, seats, rolling radius vs wheelRadius — and writes fixed appearance poses (front, side, rear, top, front34, rear34, cockpit under <out>/poses/, plus poses.jpg) and a contact sheet you must LOOK at beside your reference photos. Pass referencePaint (the median body-paint colour of the reference photos, #rrggbb) to also gate the RENDERED paint as Try Now daylight draws it: the body paint alone from six cameras with the world's own sun, exposure, tone mapping and local lights, judged on hue, saturation, lightness and highlight wash (vehicle.paint.*; a red that renders salmon or a bonnet that blows to white fails; white/silver/grey/black are judged on tint and lightness). Pass referenceWheel (a face-on close-up photo of the real wheel; optional spokeCount, finish, centreCap, crop) to also render the candidate's wheel square-on and fail vehicle.wheels.design.* on spoke count, finish or missing centre cap. It also presses every lamp key and fails vehicle.lamps.each_function_lights naming a lens that stays dark. occupants: true seats an avatar in EVERY declared seat, rear rows included (a seat the stand-in room has none of is granted in the preview's own page, so a preview is single-client), prints the CABIN FIT (where the runtime actually put each seat, and fails when it moved one more than 30 mm or refused it) and measures the cabin the way visual QA will (head clearance, hips, feet, hands on the rim, penetration). It never runs the vision critic: only a submitted or hosted visual QA is a gate result. Seats board through the candidate's OWN seat ids. OCCUPANTS AND THE GAUNTLET INSPECTION SET ARE ON BY DEFAULT: every seat is occupied and the hands are measured over time (blocking: hands_on_wheel_steering — both driver hands on the rim at centre, left lock and right lock; hands_follow_wheel — they travel round with the wheel; hands_at_nine_and_three; fingers_still and hands_still — no twitching or grasping; plus posture torso_angle, knees_up, head_in_wings), and <out>/inspection/ gets small contact sheets, one LOOK question each: exterior 8 angles day and night, each lamp lit at night, wheels, panels open, every seat from first person / side glass / over the shoulder / windscreen, the driver steering left/centre/right, and still-hands frames (preview.inspection.complete fails a set with a hole). OPEN EVERY SHEET beside the reference photos (read_skill helix-gauntlet). With item and no target and no addon it inspects a PUBLISHED car exactly as the runtime serves it. With addon: [<dir>...] it previews UNPUBLISHED add-ons instead, fitted by the engine's own fold to the candidate car or to a published car (item), and measures the DRAWN part in world space against its anchor: wheels within 1 cm of each hub, socket-framed parts on their socket, host-framed parts inside the car and not at its origin (the classic part-at-the-car-centre bug); a tune-only add-on has its ops read back from the live tuning and the v2 driveline. A host-frame add-on whose bind root/socket the car's GLB lacks is refused in under a second, before any browser (HOST_BIND_*); a runtime composition failure ('[helix-vehicle] composition failed') or page error before the car appears fails immediately with its message instead of a 120 s timeout. Needs a `helix login` (a QA account). Exit 0 pass, 1 fail, 2 could not measure.

glb.description: Absolute path to the GLB when target is a package JSON (or the directory holds several).
