inspection.description: Default true: render the gauntlet inspection set and write the contact sheets under <out>/inspection/. false only for a quick iteration (never a gate result).

referencePaint.description: The reference body paint colour (#rrggbb): the median of the body-paint pixels across several reference photos. When set, the body paint is rendered alone from six cameras in the Try Now daylight (the world's own sun, exposure, tone mapping and lights) and judged on hue, saturation, lightness and highlight wash (white, silver, grey and black are judged on tint and lightness instead). Blocking asserts vehicle.paint.hue|saturation|lightness|glare; a failure names the paint material's values and the fix (linear baseColorFactor, metallic, roughness; never exposure).

paintTolerance.description: Maximum circular hue distance in degrees the rendered body may sit from a chromatic referencePaint (default 12).

image.description: Absolute path of a face-on (or nearly) close-up photo of the REAL wheel.

spokeCount.description: Declare the real wheel's spoke count (overrides the count read from the photo; count the repeats the eye sees, a twin-spoke wheel as its pairs).

finish.description: Declare the real wheel's finish (overrides the photo).

centreCap.description: Declare whether the real wheel has a centre cap/badge (overrides the photo).

crop.description: Where the wheel sits in the photo, as fractions: centre x of the width, centre y of the height, tyre OUTER radius of the shorter side (default 0.5,0.5,0.45).

referenceWheel.description: Reference wheel close-up. When set, the candidate's front-left wheel is rendered square-on (wheelface/candidate.jpg) and judged on spoke count, finish and centre cap against the photo: blocking vehicle.wheels.design.spokes|centre_cap and .finish (a neighbouring finish only warns). Look at wheelface/candidate.jpg beside the photo.

addon.description: Absolute paths of UNPUBLISHED add-on directories (addon.json + model.glb, or no model for a tune-only part) to fit to the car and measure.

item.description: No target: the published vehicle item — alone, inspect it as the runtime serves it (the gauntlet on a listed car); with addon, the car to fit the add-ons to.

toleranceCm.description: With addon: how far a drawn part may sit from its anchor (default: wheels 1 cm, other parts 3 cm).

tools.name: check_vehicle_cabin
tools.description: Judge every declared seat of an UNPUBLISHED (or published) car's cabin OFFLINE, in about a second, with no browser and no sign-in (executes the bundled `helix vehicle cabin-check`). It fits the cabin with the platform runtime's own fitCabinToBody and seats the runtime's canonical legs at the fitted pose, measured against every triangle of the model, then reports per seat — any seat count (2, 2+2, 4, 5, 7) — H-point height over the floor, how far the runtime had to move the seat, head clearance to the roof's inner surface, knee, shin and foot clearance, the legs against the seat ahead and the tunnel/console, the rear footwell under the front seats (free height over the foot) and the driver's legs against the wheel, each PASS / WARN / FAIL with millimetres and what it is against. Iterate rear seats with this (seconds), then confirm once with preview_vehicle({ occupants: true }), which boards every seat. A WARN within a few millimetres of the seat ahead is a likely live clip (a real avatar's legs run longer than the canonical ones): clear it. Exit 0 = no FAIL (warnings may remain), 1 = a seat FAILs, 2 = could not run. validate_vehicle with cabin: true runs the same check.

target.description: Absolute path to the vehicle package directory (vehicle-package.json + model.glb) or the package JSON beside its model.

glb.description: Absolute path to the GLB when target is a package JSON (or the directory holds several).

itemId.description: Check a PUBLISHED vehicle item's stored package and drawn model instead (public read), e.g. a control car.

offline.description: Use only the cached engine runtime; never fetch it.

tools.name: check_listed_items
tools.description: Re-judge LISTED vehicles against TODAY's gates (executes the bundled `helix vehicle recheck-listed`). A listed item is never re-judged when a gate is added, so a car can be on sale on a visual-QA record that predates the gate that would fail it — the F40 was listed before the posture and hands-while-steering asserts existed, and sold with its driver lying back, hands off the wheel and fingers twitching. For each car it reads the passing record of its current version and reports CURRENT, STALE (names every current blocking gate the record never ran) or FAIL (names the gates it failed). With rerun: true it renders each car again NOW (preview_vehicle on the published car: every seat occupied, the full gauntlet inspection set and its sheets) and reports that verdict and the failing asserts. Run it before and after you update a listed car; with no itemIds it re-checks every listed vehicle (or one creator's). A STALE or FAIL car: run the helix-gauntlet loop, stage a new version of the SAME item, pass hosted visual QA, and delist it until then. Exit 0 = every car current (and passing today), 1 = a car needs action.

itemIds.description: Vehicle item ids (default: every listed vehicle in the marketplace catalogue).

creatorId.description: Without itemIds: only this creator's listed vehicles.

rerun.description: Render each car again now with today's gates (several minutes per car). Needs a `helix login` (a QA account).

out.description: With rerun: directory for each car's inspection (default ./.helix-recheck).

tools.name: import_vehicle_audio
tools.description: AUDIO STEP ONE for every vehicle, whatever its mesh source: extract the car's real recorded sound from the most accurate simulator mod (executes the bundled `helix vehicle audio-import`; minutes, FMOD bank decoding). HARD RULE: NEVER generate or synthesise vehicle sound (no resynthesis, no generate_audio, not even for a slot nothing provides, and never rely on the platform's default sounds: the synthesised fallback engine, the generated default sound pack, runtime noise); ALWAYS source real recordings, from BeamNG mods as much as possible, and a car ships a sourced recording for EVERY one of the 31 runtime slots (the only empty slots are a component the real car physically lacks, declared consumed:false, absent:"not-fitted" plus a reason, and exhaustLadder absent:"combined-with-engine" beside a sourced engine ladder; doors are required). Audio step one, whatever the mesh source: find the most accurate simulator mod of that exact car (BeamNG first; Assetto Corsa/ACC, rFactor 2, Automobilista 2 where theirs is more accurate), choose it by MEASURING candidates against real recordings of the car (firing-fundamental pitch track vs rpm, spectral centroid, roughness, idle character, limiter cadence), and extract it with import_vehicle_audio. Source: a BeamNG mod directory or .zip, an Assetto Corsa car directory or .bank, or a single .bank. It decodes the mod's engine and exhaust rpm ladders (row 0 = off-throttle/low load, row 1 = on-throttle) and its one-shots (startup, shutdown, idle, revLimiter, shiftUp/shiftDown, turboSpool, blowOff, backfire, tyreSqueal, doorOpen/doorClose, horn, intake, transmissionWhine, clutch, impacts, suspension, reverseBeep) to 16-bit PCM WAV under <out>/audio/ and writes <out>/audio.json — an `audio` block (bank + slots) to merge into vehicle-package.json — where EVERY consumed slot and bank carries provenance { kind: "sim-mod" | "sim-official" | "recording", sim, mod, modUrl?, sourceFile, sourceSha256, event?, extractor }. map is a slot-map JSON that builds one car from several sources (one mod's ladder, another mod's horn; stock events by exact take, trim, concat, real recordings, absent:"not-fitted") — read_skill helix-vehicles reference "audio-import". EVERY one of the 31 slots must come out sourced (engineLadder, exhaustLadder, idle, startup, shutdown, shiftUp, shiftDown, clutch, transmissionWhine, turboSpool, blowOff, intake, revLimiter, backfire, suspension, impactLight, impactMedium, impactHeavy, tyreSqueal, tyreScrub, tyreSpin, tyreRollSlow, tyreRollFast, indicatorTick, skid, brakeSqueal, handbrake, reverseBeep, horn, doorOpen, doorClose); a slot the best mod lacks is filled, in order, from another BeamNG mod of the same engine or car family, the BeamNG base game's stock banks and vehicles/common sounds, another simulator's mod, real recordings of the car — never another car's sound, never synthesised, never a platform default. The only permitted empty slots are a component the real car physically lacks (turboSpool/blowOff without a turbo, reverseBeep, clutch on an automatic/CVT, EV combustion slots), declared consumed:false, absent:"not-fitted" plus a reason, and exhaustLadder absent:"combined-with-engine" beside a sourced engine ladder when the mod records one combined set. Doors are required. HOW TO PICK THE MOST ACCURATE MOD: measure every candidate against real recordings of the car — firing-fundamental pitch track vs rpm, spectral centroid, roughness/harmonic balance, idle character, limiter cadence — with the commands in read_skill({ name: "helix-vehicles", reference: "audio" }), never by reputation. Writes <out>/audio.json (all 31 slots, plus the five mix fields the runtime reads: from the map, basePackage, the mod's soundConfig, else engine defaults) and <out>/audio-import.json (the report: every slot's decision, source, alternatives and reason, and the unmapped source sounds). Then run check_vehicle_audio. Exit 0 = every slot written with provenance; 1 = the source could not be read, yielded no engine audio, or left slots unfilled (the output lists them). Answers NOT AVAILABLE when the bundled CLI has no audio-import command (it never improvises a synthesised substitute).

out.description: Absolute path of the vehicle package directory to write audio/*.wav and audio.json into.

sim.description: Which simulator the source is from (default auto-detect).

vehicle.description: BeamNG vehicle id inside the mod (when it holds several).

config.description: BeamNG configuration (.pc file) whose soundConfig is wanted; a trim can use a different engine blend.

map.description: Absolute path to a slot-map JSON merging slots from several sources into one car.

beamngRoot.description: Absolute path to the BeamNG.drive install (or set HELIX_BEAMNG_ROOT), so stock FMOD banks and engine blends a mod refers to by name (art_sound.zip, audio.zip, vehicles/common.zip) resolve and slots no part names get what the game itself plays.

cylinders.description: The RECORDED engine's cylinder count (the ladder pitch model). Derived from a BeamNG engine part when it says; REQUIRED for an Assetto Corsa car and for a BeamNG mod whose count would only be a guess.

prefer.description: Microphone set to prefer when the source has both (default exterior).

acNativeRungs.description: Assetto Corsa: keep only rungs recorded at their own reference rpm (no FMOD auto-pitch varispeed).

basePackage.description: Absolute path to an existing vehicle-package.json, its directory, or an audio.json: its audio block supplies the mix (engineGainDb, exhaustGainDb, minLoadMix, maxLoadMix, muffling) so re-importing a PUBLISHED car keeps its current mix. Use it whenever the car already exists.

modUrl.description: Where the mod was fetched from; recorded in every slot's provenance.

tools.name: check_vehicle_audio
tools.description: Prove every sound a vehicle declares will actually play, is SOURCED (real recordings with provenance, never synthesised) AND sounds like an engine — the silent-car check visual QA never makes (executes the bundled `helix vehicle audio-check`). PROVENANCE: it prints, for every slot and bank, its source — sim, mod, url, source file, sha256, extractor — and REFUSES synthesised or generated audio (AUDIO_SYNTHESISED), FAILS a car without sourced engine audio, i.e. one that would fall back to the engine's built-in synthesised engine (AUDIO_ENGINE_UNSOURCED), and FAILS any EMPTY slot and any slot that would fall back to a platform default (the generated default sound pack, synthetic starter, runtime tyre/skid/handbrake noise) — all 31 slots must be sourced (AUDIO_SLOT_UNSOURCED); the only permitted empty slots are a component the real car physically lacks (turbo slots on an NA car, reverseBeep, clutch on an automatic/CVT, EV combustion slots and, on a single-speed drive, shiftUp/shiftDown; transmissionWhine stays required; an EV is detected from physics, its motor ladder is a recording, and audio.drivetrain:"electric" FAILS as AUDIO_SYNTHESISED), declared consumed:false, absent:"not-fitted" plus a reason, and exhaustLadder absent:"combined-with-engine" beside a sourced engine ladder. Also refused: AUDIO_MIX_FIELDS_MISSING (engineGainDb/exhaustGainDb missing or non-finite, or minLoadMix/maxLoadMix/muffling outside 0..1 — a car shipped without them froze in Try Now), AUDIO_PROVENANCE_MISSING (a recording that says nothing about its origin) and AUDIO_SLOT_FITMENT_MISMATCH (a not-fitted claim the physics contradicts, or turbo sounds on a non-turbo car). The fix is import_vehicle_audio from the most accurate simulator mod (then the BeamNG base game, another sim, real recordings), never synthesis. It selects samples exactly as the engine does (every rung of the engineBlend/exhaustBlend ladders, and each slot asset named by its buffers) and requires each to resolve (pre-publish: a WAV beside the package; published: HTTP 200 with the exact declared bytes and sha256), to be PCM WAV, and to be audible rather than digital silence. A cid-only row, a 404, a re-encoded file or an MP3 each fail. Three further gates: every ladder rung's measured fundamental must match its rpm label against the firing fundamental for the declared sampleCylinderCount/strokes/crankLayout (a rung an octave or more off is refused — the round-7 octave-low ladders), engine and exhaust must be separate sourced recordings (a mod with ONE combined recording omits exhaustBlend and declares exhaustLadder absent:"combined-with-engine"; both blends on one sourced recording is only a warning, AUDIO_ENGINE_EXHAUST_SHARED_RECORDING), and each rung must be a real broadband engine sound, not a near-pure synthetic tone (measured by autocorrelation and spectral noise floor; a beep passes pitch but fails this). CONTENT GATES (thresholds calibrated so the 993, recorded horns and field recordings pass): AUDIO_CLIPPED (flat-topped runs at full scale or at the file's own peak), AUDIO_DC_OFFSET, AUDIO_LADDER_FIXED_FORMANTS (one resonator stack stamped on every rung), AUDIO_LADDER_FIXED_TONE (a fixed-frequency line in most rungs), AUDIO_LADDER_RUNG_COPY (a rung resampled from its neighbour) and AUDIO_HORN_SYNTHETIC (an exactly periodic horn, warn) — read_skill helix-vehicles reference "audio", "Content gates". Also refused: two roles that are one recording (shift up = shift down, horn = an engine rung, an exhaust rung = an engine rung resampled), and a rev-limiter sample longer than 0.35 s (the runtime re-fires it every 60 ms, so a long clip plays as a held tone). Pass `reference` (a recording of the real car idling) to compare your idle voice with it. Pass a package directory/JSON before publishing, or a published vehicle item id to read back what the runtime gets. Exit 0 = every sample plays, is sourced and is a real engine sound; 1 = a sample will not play, a slot is empty or unsourced, audio is synthesised, or a gate fails.

target.description: Absolute path to the package directory or vehicle-package.json (pre-publish), or a published vehicle item UUID (read-back).

reference.description: Recordings of the REAL car to compare the idle voice with: an absolute path to a WAV (mp3/m4a/ogg need ffmpeg) of the engine idling, or "slot=/abs/path" for a named slot (horn=, startup=, ...). Several clips: the median is compared. Spectral centroid and firing roughness; warning beyond x2.5, error beyond x10.

tools.name: check_vehicle_addon
tools.description: Prove a vehicle add-on will fit and LAND WHERE IT SHOULD before it is published (executes the bundled `helix vehicle addon check`). Directory: addon.json { title, fits, ops, description?, tags?, version?, provenance? } + model.glb (tune-only parts ship none). Checks: the fits/ops contract (at most 32 ops; 64 for a clip-set), the model's scene.extras.helixMeshFrame (a socket-frame part must be centred on its mount — the hub for wheels), and per host: it is a vehicle, its drawn wheel origins are AT THE HUBS, every hide glob matches a host node, the host board GRANTS the hide (the standard board grants only *_stock_* globs, so a wheel hiding rim_* fits ZERO hosts until the host grants it) and EXPOSES every tunable path the part requires; then the backend's own fit dry run reports how many hosts it really fits; and for `tune` ops the DRIVE EFFECT on each host, measured with the live runtime's own physics and add-on fold (0-100, top speed, quarter mile, skidpad g and body roll, 60-0 at full and 30% pedal, handbrake), each op judged on a figure it can move — a part that changes nothing is an error, an op that cancels another a warning. A performance-slot part (engine, ECU, gearbox, exhaust, brakes, suspension, anti-roll bars, intake) with NO tune op and no sound mount is refused up front (round 5's "competition exhaust" did nothing). It also runs the web customizer's own meshless guard on the exact add-on definition publish would seal: a part with no model.glb must be a verified tune-only (or sound-only) definition, otherwise the customizer refuses to equip or save it and the check reports ADDON_CUSTOMIZER_REFUSES with the customizer's exact message (round 8 sold four tune-only parts that every older check called fit). The drive effect is measured ungoverned (speedLimiterKph is ignored; no add-on can add or remove a speed limiter). Exit 0 = fits every named host and does something.

dir.description: Absolute path to the add-on directory.

glb.description: Absolute path to the add-on model when the directory holds more than one .glb.

noMeasure.description: Skip the drive-effect measurement of tune ops.

tools.name: publish_vehicle_addon
tools.description: Publish a vehicle add-on end to end from its directory, Package-first (executes the bundled `helix vehicle addon publish`; minutes): the full check_vehicle_addon (including the drive-effect measurement) → upload the model (none for a tune-only part) → seal a public `addon` Package → make the Item from that exact Version (pinned at birth, unlisted, no offer) → read back (pinned, the backend lists every host as a fit, it appears on each host's add-on rail). A hide the host has not granted stops it: the host car must seal the grant (hostGrantExtensions in its publish.json). Sell it with create_item_distribution once visual QA passes. Resumable. Exit 0 = published and verified. itemId + version publishes a changed part as a NEW VERSION of the same item (staged, then moved; a listed meshed part is held by visual QA: stage, run visual QA on that version, repeat the same call to finish). dryRun also runs the seal's refusals (provenance.source <= 256 chars, contentRating, title/tag limits, Package shape, version clash). Answers NOT AVAILABLE when the bundled CLI has no add-on mint.

dir.description: Absolute path to the add-on directory.

glb.description: Absolute path to the add-on model when the directory holds more than one .glb.

noMeasure.description: Skip the drive-effect measurement of tune ops.

itemId.description: Publish a NEW VERSION of this existing add-on item instead of minting one (needs version).

version.description: Package Version to seal, MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH; with itemId, the next version of that part (e.g. 1.0.1). A version name already sealed with different bytes is refused.

reason.description: With itemId: the audited version-move reason, 1-500 chars (default names the version).

dryRun.description: Run the check and the seal-side validation only; nothing is uploaded.

tools.name: visual_qa_item
tools.description: Runs the bundled CLI (`helix item visual-qa`) and returns its output and exit code: renders a published item's CURRENT package version headless in the real HELIX runtime (test-grounds world for vehicles AND whole avatars — the avatar is tried on as the player and walked —, the customiser for add-ons and wearables on every declared host/base, the item viewer for props, the item page for emotes, the Home walk-through for scenes), measures it (wheels at hubs, arch clearance, socket placement, on-body bounds, scale, NaN/invisible, textured; for avatars also materials resolved, no emissive wash-out, lit colour vs its own base colour, limb twist and skin tearing while walking), and with --submit records the backend's verdict — numeric asserts plus a vision critic — against that exact version, with a contact sheet. Marketplace/Vault listing, Marketplace/World distributions and version moves on a public item REQUIRE a passing record: run this after every publish or new version, read the reasons and the contact sheet, fix the item, and re-run. Exit code 0 = pass, 1 = fail, 2 = harness error (fails closed; never a pass and never overridable for an avatar). An avatar stays HELD (visible only to its creator) until this passes for its current version. To have the platform render it instead of this machine, use visual_qa_item_hosted.

itemId.description: Universal item id to render and judge.

submit.description: Record the verdict on the backend (default true). False = local dry run only.

localCritic.description: Also run the vision critic locally (needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENROUTER_API_KEY in the environment).

storageState.description: Playwright storageState JSON of a signed-in QA account; Try Now and the customiser need one (default $HELIX_VQA_STORAGE_STATE).

hostIds.description: Only fit onto these host/base item ids (add-ons, wearables). Default: every declared host/base.

packageVersion.description: Judge this candidate Package Version instead of the current one — a version move on an already-offered item must pass here BEFORE the move.

vehiclePackage.description: With packageVersion, for a vehicle: path to the candidate vehicle-package JSON the version will carry.

tools.name: visual_qa_item_hosted
tools.description: Runs the bundled CLI (`helix item visual-qa --hosted`) and returns its output and exit code: asks the PLATFORM to render and judge an item's current package version on its hosted GPU runner — no Chrome, no GPU, no QA login on your machine. It queues one hosted run per (item, package version, manifest), waits, and exits 0 = passed, 1 = failed (reasons printed), 2 = error / timed out, printing the contact sheet URL. Use this instead of visual_qa_item when this machine has no suitable browser (CI, a sandbox, a remote agent), or after a VISUAL_QA_REQUIRED refusal / deferred Marketplace publish, which already queue a hosted run for you (the response carries hostedRun: { jobId, status }; follow it with visual_qa_item_status). A passing hosted run satisfies the same listing gate as a local --submit run. A freshly sealed model can lag the CDN; the runner waits for it (<=10 min) and a lag never uses an attempt. Retry (requeue a fresh job) after a failed/errored/exhausted run only once the item is fixed or the failure was infrastructure (retry:true).

itemId.description: Universal item id to render and judge on the hosted runner.

retry.description: REQUEUE this exact version after a failed, errored or exhausted hosted run: a fresh job whose attempts start again (waits out the server cooldown, ~10 min after the last run, up to timeoutMinutes). Use after infrastructure/mirror failures or once a fix is published as a new version.

wait.description: Wait for the verdict (default true). False = queue it and return; read it later with visual_qa_item_status.

timeoutMinutes.description: How long to wait for the verdict (default 30).

tools.name: visual_qa_item_status
tools.description: Runs the bundled CLI (`helix item visual-qa --status`, read-only) and returns an item's hosted visual-QA state: the latest hosted job for its CURRENT package version (queued / rendering / passed / failed / error, attempts, reasons, error), the contact sheet URL, and whether the current version has a passing run. Needs no login and changes nothing. Exit code 0 = passed or still in flight/none, 1 = failed, 2 = error. Use it to follow a hostedRun from a VISUAL_QA_REQUIRED refusal or a deferred publish.

itemId.description: Universal item id whose hosted visual-QA state to read.

tools.name: delist_item
tools.description: Runs the bundled CLI (`helix item delist`). Unlist a published item DEFINITION the creator owns (CH-1671). Existing owners keep what they already have; the item stops appearing on browse/marketplace and nobody new can acquire it through ANY of its distributions. This is not a delete: owned item definitions remain so current owners keep their content. Different from disable_item_distribution, which only turns off ONE acquisition route. Not currently reversible (no relist).

itemId.description: The universal item id to delist — the UUID from the item detail page/API or an approved Creator publication receipt.

reason.description: Optional note for the creator's own record; not shown to anyone else.

tools.name: item_thumbnail
tools.description: Refresh or replace the thumbnail of an ALREADY-PUBLISHED item (avatar, wearable, add-on, vehicle, ...) you own — runs in-process, no CLI step. action=refresh re-renders the canonical thumbnail from the item's ACTIVE Package Version with the standard server renderer (use after a corrected Package Version, or when the thumbnail still shows an older mesh); pass dryRun first to see what would change without writing, and force to re-render when the server says it is already current. action=set uploads your own png/jpg/webp (imagePath) — moderated, and it is kept across version moves until a later refresh with force. To correct a Package-backed avatar mesh, seal a new Package Version and move the item onto it, then refresh here. A creator-owned item only (403 otherwise); an older backend answers 'does not support thumbnail refresh yet'. Not for worlds: use set_world_thumbnail.

action.description: refresh = server re-render from the active Package Version; set = upload your own image

itemId.description: Published universal item id (UUID) from the item detail page/API or an approved Creator publication receipt.

force.description: refresh only: re-render even when the stored thumbnail is already current

dryRun.description: refresh only: report what would change, write nothing

imagePath.description: set only: absolute path to a png/jpg/jpeg/webp image (up to 10 MiB)

tools.name: create_item_distribution
tools.description: Runs the bundled CLI (`helix item distribution create`) and returns its output: creates one creator-authorized primary Claim/Buy route for a published item. This does not republish the definition or charge another publish fee. World routes require the owned world slug plus a stable key; Marketplace routes carry neither. LISTING IS SHIPPING: do not call this before the helix-gauntlet loop has PASSED on the published item (for a vehicle: preview_vehicle({ item }) with every inspection sheet looked at and every occupant assert passing, and check_listed_items({ itemIds: [itemId] }) CURRENT). The CLI REFUSES a vehicle whose current version's visual-QA record did not run, or did not pass, every blocking gate of today (it names the gates); there is no override here — fix the car, stage a new version and pass visual_qa_item_hosted.

priceLix.description: 0 = Claim; positive = Buy and must meet the server-owned floor.

world.description: Owned world slug, required for channel=world.

key.description: Stable world code key, required for channel=world.

tools.name: list_item_distributions
tools.description: Runs the bundled CLI (`helix item distribution list --json`) and returns every active or disabled primary distribution drawing from one item definition.

tools.name: update_item_distribution
tools.description: Runs the bundled CLI (`helix item distribution update`): reprices or changes schedule/caps on an existing distribution. Item, channel, world and stable key are immutable. Pass unlimited to clear a cap and none to clear a schedule boundary.

tools.name: disable_item_distribution
tools.description: Runs the bundled CLI (`helix item distribution disable`): disables an acquisition route without deleting its history or item definition.

tools.name: scaffold_item_definition
tools.description: RETURNS A COMMAND, NOT DATA. This tool hands you a `helix …` command string to RUN yourself — it executes nothing and returns no results. The answer is in that command’s output. Prepare the CLI command that authors a COMPLETE, valid interactive item definition — no hand-written descriptor JSON. Two item types, and the type decides which arguments apply. type:"weapon" (the default) builds it from a mesh plus a category (Rifle | Pistol | SMG | Shotgun | Sniper | LMG | Launcher | Grenade), which resolves the engine spread and reload tables, the grip preset and the shell class; with no sounds directory it copies category-default shot sounds next to the descriptor. The two explosive categories also carry the fire kind: a Launcher fires a projectile round, a Grenade is THROWN and is never rack-equipped — the blast itself (damage fanout, the fuse, the FX) stays world-authored, read_doc({name:"shooter-worlds"}) section 9. Mesh convention: grip point at the ORIGIN, +y up, +z out the barrel, meters. type:"emote" builds it from an animation clip GLB instead: the performance IS the item, so there is no mesh, no category and no gun config, and the clip has a hard duration ceiling — 10s as playback "oneshot", 60s as playback "loop". A PAIRED emote (one another player joins in on) adds a second clip, where that player stands, and an optional offerAtS — the pose the initiator holds while waiting, as seconds into their own clip. Either playback pairs. The scaffold prints the exact roles block to paste in, or pass joinerClip + joinerOffset + offerAt to the descriptor. An emote may also carry TRANSITIONS: introClipPath is the enter clip played into the body clip, outroClipPath the exit clip played out of it (a sit-down before a sit loop, a stand-up after it). Each caps at 5s, and on playback "oneshot" intro + clip + outro together cap at the same 10s — the player is locked for the whole chain. A PAIRED emote takes NEITHER: a joiner arrives on a held offer, so there is no shared instant to chain a transition into. Follow with validate_item_definition. This legacy descriptor format has no Item-first publishing route; use the approved sealed-Package publication flow for new content. For the consumption side (installWeaponItem before attach), read_doc({name:"shooter-worlds"}) section 8.

type.description: Item type. Default: weapon. A weapon takes meshPath + category; an emote takes clipPath + playback.

meshPath.description: WEAPON: path to the prop mesh .glb. Required unless type is "emote".

category.description: WEAPON: archetype — it inherits spread, reload foley, grip preset and shell class, and for Launcher/Grenade the projectile or thrown fire kind. Required unless type is "emote"; an emote has no category.

soundsDir.description: WEAPON: directory of your own .ogg shot sounds (mono opus-in-ogg; a file named *dry* becomes the dry-fire click). Omit for the category defaults.

clipPath.description: EMOTE: path to the animation .glb the emote plays. Required when type is "emote".

playback.description: EMOTE: how the clip plays. Default: oneshot. A oneshot clip caps at 10 seconds, a loop at 60 — validate MEASURES the clip and refuses one that overruns its mode.

audioPath.description: EMOTE: one .ogg the performance carries (mono opus-in-ogg). Optional.

introClipPath.description: EMOTE: path to the ENTER transition .glb, played once into the body clip (e.g. the sit-down before a sitting loop). Caps at 5s, and on playback "oneshot" it counts against the 10s ceiling for intro + clip + outro. Not allowed on a paired emote.

outroClipPath.description: EMOTE: path to the EXIT transition .glb, played once out of the body clip (e.g. the stand-up after a sitting loop). Same 5s cap and the same "oneshot" chain ceiling, and likewise not allowed on a paired emote.

title.description: Item title, also the source of the item id. Default: the mesh/clip basename.

outDir.description: Output directory for the descriptor plus copied files. Default: the current directory.

tools.name: validate_item_definition
tools.description: RETURNS A COMMAND, NOT DATA. This tool hands you a `helix …` command string to RUN yourself — it executes nothing and returns no results. The answer is in that command’s output. Prepare the CLI command that validates an item descriptor OFFLINE: the manifest authority validator, the vendored rules for the descriptor type, referenced-file existence, and the mesh precheck. A weapon is checked against the engine gun-config rules; an emote is checked against its own — the emote block and a resolvable clip, no gun config, and the MEASURED clip duration against its playback ceiling (10s oneshot, 60s loop). A PAIRED emote (an emote.roles.joiner block) is checked the same way on BOTH clips, plus the joiner offset bounds and the offer instant, which must land inside the measured initiator clip. Enter/exit TRANSITIONS (emote.intro / emote.outro) are measured too — 5s each, and on a "oneshot" intro + clip + outro together against the 10s ceiling — and are refused outright on a paired emote. Run it after any hand edit.

tools.name: inspect_item_definition
tools.description: RETURNS A COMMAND, NOT DATA. This tool hands you a `helix …` command string to RUN yourself — it executes nothing and returns no results. The answer is in that command’s output. Prepare the CLI command that resolves a PUBLISHED item definition and prints what an author tunes against — a weapon cadence, ammo, damage, spread and sounds; an emote its playback mode and pinned clip, plus the joiner clip and offset when it is a paired one. Read-only.

assetId.description: Asset ID of an already-published legacy weapon or emote definition.

version.description: Pin a specific version. Default: the latest.

tools.name: scaffold_locomotion_pack
tools.description: RETURNS A COMMAND, NOT DATA. This tool hands you a `helix …` command string to RUN yourself — it executes nothing and returns no results. The answer is in that command’s output. Prepare the CLI command that writes a STARTER locomotion pack directory — anims/clip-meta.json seeded with one example walk entry plus a README carrying the per-clip contract (the full clip vocabulary lives in read_doc({name:"locomotion-clip-spec"})). A locomotion pack is the set of replacement movement clips a player equips as a character add-on (a female walk, a zombie shamble): data, not code, in the `character.locomotion@1` slot. Then drop your authored GLBs beside the meta file (file name = the entry name + ".glb", exactly one animation per file, arriving in-place on canonical helix-humanoid bones) and add an entry per clip this pack ships, each with its MEASURED duration and strideSpeed — a single-clip pack is a legitimate product, and every name it omits falls back to the platform clip. Read the spec doc first; follow with validate_locomotion_pack. Item-first pack publishing is retired.

dir.description: Directory for the new pack; the starter files land in <dir>/anims/.

overwrite.description: Replace starter files that already exist. Default: existing files are KEPT and reported as skipped, so re-scaffolding never clobbers an authored clip-meta.json.

tools.name: validate_locomotion_pack
tools.description: RETURNS A COMMAND, NOT DATA. This tool hands you a `helix …` command string to RUN yourself — it executes nothing and returns no results. The answer is in that command’s output. Prepare the CLI command that validates a locomotion pack directory OFFLINE and reports EVERY problem in one pass, not just the first: the pack format (anims/clip-meta.json present, readable and an array; per-entry name/loop/duration/strideSpeed types), the GLB cross-checks (a file per surviving entry, exactly one animation in it, its real length against the declared duration), the gait-only clip vocabulary (deaths, get-ups and sit/lie poses are refused in a pack), the strideSpeed rules — null on the non-travelling clips, the per-clip band around the platform reference on the travelling ones — and the walk < run < sprint ladder across the gaits the pack actually contains. A ring clip with no direction, or a direction off the fixed grid, is reported as a warning: it loads but never joins the strafe ring. Run it after any hand edit to clip-meta.json.

dir.description: Path to the pack directory (the one containing anims/).

tools.name: list_my_worlds
tools.description: List the worlds owned by the logged-in creator (including drafts), with their slugs and build state.

tools.name: create_world
tools.description: Mint a world's IDENTITY — the row, as a Draft with no build — so products and achievements can be registered BEFORE the first publish. Both registries live outside the bundle and hang off a world id, so on a brand-new project register_world_product and register_achievement fail with "No world of yours has the slug ..." until this has run; publishing is what adds a build, not what creates the world. Idempotent for a slug you already own — the existing world is reported and nothing is sent; a slug someone else owns is refused by the backend. The slug is globally unique and permanent, so choose it once.

slug.description: URL identifier: 3-50 chars, lowercase letters/digits/hyphens, starting alphanumeric. Globally unique and PERMANENT.

title.description: Display name players see, max 80 chars

serverCreationPermission.description: Who may stand up a persistent server for this world (server default: anyone)

tools.name: register_achievement
tools.description: Register an achievement on one of the creator's worlds — the registry a world's badges live in, which is NOT part of helix.json and cannot be declared in the bundle. REGISTER BEFORE PUBLISHING the rule that awards it: `awardAchievement` with an unregistered key publishes clean and is a silent runtime no-op, the single most common authoring trap. Needs a 2D icon file (required — an achievement always has a graphic; generate one with generate_image if the human has no art, and note that a blank or sub-16px placeholder is refused). Leave unlockMode alone for a badge a room rule awards (the default); declare `signal` + `value` instead for a criteria badge the backend measures with no room at all. Pass dryRun to validate everything locally — no network, works logged out. TEST THE UNLOCK FIRST: the same row seeds `.helix/dev-achievements.json` for `helix dev`, where a criteria badge unlocks off simulated evidence as you play — the seed uses the STORED nested shape (`criteria: { signal, op, value, key, field, metric }`; this tool flattens `key`/`field` into criteriaKey/criteriaField because `key` is already the badge slug) and needs no icon. Registration takes effect immediately, live worlds included — no republish; the backfill pass credits players who already qualify.

worldSlug.description: Slug of the world that issues the achievement (the creator owns it)

key.description: Stable slug your rules name: 2-80 chars, lowercase a-z0-9_-, starting alphanumeric. Treat it as a schema — renaming needs a fresh registration.

icon.description: Absolute path to the 2D graphic (png/jpg/webp/gif/avif/heic) — REQUIRED

description.description: What the player did to earn it

hidden.description: Show "???" until the player earns it

trophy.description: Absolute path to a bespoke 3D trophy (.glb); omitted, the icon is baked onto the default plaque

unlockMode.description: Who may award it — the trust marker. Default: `criteria` when a signal is declared, else `room` (an awardAchievement rule). `platform` means FIRST-PARTY code awards it: nothing in a world can, so do not pick it.

signal.description: Declaring a signal makes this a `criteria` achievement (the backend measures it, no room needed — works single-player). datastore = a numeric field in a per-user document; iwp = in-world purchases; analytics = a platform event count; playtime = seconds in this world.

value.description: Threshold the measured value is compared against. Required with `signal`.

criteriaKey.description: datastore only, and this IS the trust decision: "mp:player:{userId}" is the room's flushed persistent playerVars (room-written ⇒ trustworthy), "player:{userId}" is the player's own client-written save (they can write it ⇒ self-reported).

criteriaField.description: datastore only: dot-path to the number (e.g. "stats.summits"). For mp:player:{userId} it names the persistent playerVar directly.

eventName.description: analytics only: the PLATFORM analytics event to count (e.g. world_entered). A world cannot mint its own.

metric.description: iwp only: purchase count (default) or total LIX spent.

dryRun.description: Validate locally and report what would be sent; no network, no login needed

tools.name: list_achievements
tools.description: List a world's registered achievements. Run it BEFORE publishing multiplayer rules to confirm every key an `awardAchievement` effect names actually exists — publish cannot check the registry, and a missing key fails silently at runtime.

tools.name: update_achievement
tools.description: Patch a registered achievement's presentation (name/description/points/hidden/active). The key, unlock mode and criteria are FIXED at registration — rules name the key, and re-labelling how a badge is earned would rewrite what every already-granted copy claims; register a new achievement instead. To change the ICON ART in place, use set_achievement_icon (the key and every holder's badge are preserved — do NOT re-register just to swap art). Set active:false to delist one (existing holders keep theirs).

active.description: false delists it — nobody new can earn it

tools.name: set_achievement_icon
tools.description: Replace a registered achievement's ICON ART in place (HYPR-5142). Same UniversalItem, same key — every holder keeps their badge, and the default trophy plaque is re-baked with the new art (a bespoke trophy mesh is left untouched). This is the RIGHT way to change art: do NOT re-register the achievement to swap an icon (that re-keys it and leaves the old one delisted). `image` is a path to a local icon file (png/jpeg/webp); it is validated (a single flat colour is rejected) before anything is uploaded.

image.description: Path to the replacement icon image file (png/jpeg/webp)

tools.name: register_world_product
tools.description: Register a product one of the creator's worlds SELLS — the registry `Helix.marketplace.purchaseProduct` buys from, which is NOT part of helix.json and cannot be declared in the bundle or minted at runtime. REGISTER BEFORE WRITING the code that buys it: world code names the creator-authored `key` (`purchaseProduct("speed_boost")` buys `pkey:speed_boost`) and the key is IMMUTABLE once registered, so it is chosen here, once. The PRICE lives server-side only — a world never sends an amount; the shell raises the confirm popup and settles. priceLix 0 is legitimate: it registers a free "Claim". AUTHOR WHAT IT HANDS OVER as a `grants` effect array — pass | currency; several effects = a bundle, an empty array = a tip jar. The backend fulfils it DURABLY at settle. World Products do not mint universal Items; use the Creator approved Publications workflow for those. The effect list is IMMUTABLE once registered. Pass dryRun to validate everything locally — no network, works logged out. TEST THE LOOP FIRST: the same product row seeds `.helix/dev-products.json` for `helix dev` — buy/entitlements/consume answer locally with nothing charged, and the debug menu forces the failure paths. Registration takes effect on a live world immediately — no republish.

worldSlug.description: Slug of the world that sells it (the creator owns it). Registering on a draft world is allowed; a purchase needs a live world.

title.description: Name the purchase popup shows the player (max 120 chars)

type.description: Legacy world-local effect with no durable grant. Universal-item grant types are not creator-facing.

passKey.description: pass only: entitlement name (defaults to the product key; required if the product has no key). Lowercase a-z0-9_-

durationSeconds.description: pass only: timed pass length; re-purchase extends from the current expiry. Omit = permanent

code.description: currency only: balance name (lowercase a-z0-9_-, max 64; a world may mint at most 16 distinct codes)

amount.description: currency only: how much one purchase adds

display.description: currency only: UI hint — a wallet ("740 coins") or consumable uses ("x5 potions"). Same behavior either way

grants.description: The world-local effect array is IMMUTABLE once registered. Max 8 effects; several = a bundle, [] = a tip jar. Universal items use ItemDistribution instead.

priceLix.description: Price in LIX. 0 registers a free "Claim" — a confirmation, no spend. This is the ONLY place a price lives.

key.description: Required stable slug world code buys as `pkey:<key>`: max 64 chars of lowercase a-z0-9_-, starting alphanumeric. IMMUTABLE — renaming would break every build naming it. Internal product UUIDs are never purchase references.

description.description: What the player is buying (max 2000 chars)

maxPerUser.description: Cap on how many one player may own (whole number >= 1). A permanent-pass-only product is capped at 1 and REFUSES a higher value — a re-buy would charge again and deliver nothing.

dryRun.description: Validate locally and report what would be sent; no network, no login needed

tools.name: list_world_products
tools.description: List what a world sells: each registered product, the `pkey:<key>` world code buys it by, its price and whether it is still on sale. Run it BEFORE writing purchase code to confirm the key you are about to name exists — an unregistered key fails only at runtime, as ProductNotFound. Omit worldSlug for every PUBLISHED world of the creator's and its registry (that route lists Published worlds only, so name the slug to see a draft world's).

worldSlug.description: Slug of the world; omit for all your published worlds and what each sells

tools.name: update_world_product
tools.description: Patch a registered product's presentation, price or ownership cap, or set active:false to take it off sale (the row stays, so past purchases and the items they granted keep resolving). The key and the type are FIXED at registration — world code buys the key, and changing what a purchase hands over would re-label every copy already sold; register a new product and deactivate this one instead.

worldSlug.description: Slug of the world that sells it

product.description: The product key (or its uuid, if it was registered without a key)

priceLix.description: New price in LIX; 0 makes it a free "Claim"

maxPerUser.description: New per-player ownership cap (whole number >= 1). Refused above 1 on a permanent-pass-only product; pass null to clear it back to the derived cap.

active.description: false takes it off sale — existing owners keep theirs, nobody new can buy it

tools.name: import_character
tools.description: Convert an external biped character GLB (a Meshy AI export, or any Mixamo-named rig) into a helix-humanoid@1 character asset. Conforms the mesh onto the canonical skeleton AT ITS OWN PROPORTIONS (the platform’s shared locomotion clips then drive it), generates the LOD chain (micro-chart baked atlases are auto-rebaked: weld → re-unwrap → closest-point texture transfer), and KTX2-encodes the textures — all in-process, no native tools, no extra files (the canonical helix-humanoid@1 skeleton is bundled; a world’s installed humanoid-character pack or `canonical` overrides it). Outputs <output>/<name>.web.glb (multi-scene: scene i = LOD i; the head is sliced into a FaceMesh node per level so first-person mode can hide it, like the stock face part), plus <output>/anims/<clipName>.glb when `anim` is given. Use when the human supplies a custom character model instead of the stock bodies. For a PUBLISHED AVATAR item (any source: VRM, generated, game model, robot) follow the helix-avatars skill — get_started({kind:"avatar"}) — which covers rigging, budgets over all LODs, hair/cloth physics and the QA that catches what every gate misses. FACES: the import prints a `face:` line — read it. Detection only recognizes exact established morph names (viseme_*, vrc.v_*, aa/ih/ou/ee/oh, jawOpen, blinkLeft/Blink_L), so a rig whose shapes are named anything else — a VRoid model exported as GLB rather than VRM (Fcl_MTH_A, Fcl_EYE_Close_L, …) is the common case — imports as `face: none` and that avatar is PERMANENTLY MUTE, with no error anywhere. Pass `faceMap` to map the semantics onto the morphs the asset actually has. A .vrm source should go through bridge_import instead, which carries the vowels, blinks and expressions across on its own. read_doc({name:"avatar-face"}) has the mapping file and the capability ladder. Validated example — a Meshy AI character with its walk animation, everything else default: { "body": "C:/downloads/Meshy_AI_Warrior_biped_Character_output.glb", "anim": "C:/downloads/Meshy_AI_Warrior_biped_Animation_Walking_withSkin.glb", "name": "warrior", "output": "./characters" } → characters/warrior.web.glb (~3MB, LOD tris ≈10000/5000/1500 at 1024/512/256px KTX2, UASTC up close + ETC1S far) + characters/anims/locomotion.warriorWalk.glb.

Run it in the world project after `npm install` and after every pin edit, before `npm run build`. Replays the committed helix.lock.json when present; pass update:true to re-resolve ranges to newer versions and rewrite the lock — also REQUIRED after adding a new pin (e.g. visual) to a world that already has a lock. Same code path as the human `helix install`, but resolution happens in-process against THIS toolchain's environment — no PATH ambiguity.

tools.name: list_abilities

system.description: Only abilities targeting this system id (e.g. humanoid-character)

tools.name: get_package_manifest
tools.description: Fetch the full manifest for a published system/ability/asset-pack — the contract to read before pinning OR configuring it. For a SYSTEM, the payload carries `config` (the complete tunable surface) + `capabilities`. For an ABILITY, ability.json with its configSchema. Always includes the code + asset CDN base URLs. Defaults to the latest version. Read this instead of guessing config keys.

version.description: Semver version; defaults to the latest published version

tools.name: list_materials
tools.description: FIRST ASSET RUNG: search the versioned HELIX platform material pack. Returns the offered PBR texture materials (photographed or scanned; procedural glass/water are not offered and are named under `unlisted`) and the immutable CDN base as JSON. Use before Vault search, generation, or external/CC0 sources. Apply one with use_material.

query.description: Free-text material search over id, name, category, and tags

category.description: Exact category filter, e.g. brick, wood, metal, glass

limit.description: Palette budget for this result (default 12; the global catalog remains open-ended)

resolution.description: texture resolution, e.g. 1k or 2k; omit for the material's default. Keeps only materials carrying it. The CLI errors with the valid values rather than substituting a different resolution.

tools.name: use_material
tools.description: Resolve one HELIX platform material id to its immutable CDN map URLs, its `assetBaseUrl` and its authored rendering defaults, at the texture resolution you pick. APPLY IT with the visual system, never by hand: pin `"visual": "^0.1"` in helix.json (then install_world_packages with update: true), `const materials = await loadMaterialLibrary(assetBaseUrl, { renderer })` from @helix/visual, `materials.apply(mesh, id)` — exact per-axis tiling for boxes, planes, spheres, cylinders and capsules; pass `{ size: [w, h] }` (metres the 0..1 UV span covers) for imported meshes — then `await materials.ready()`. Details: read_doc({ name: "world-look" }). The output states which resolution was resolved and which ones the material offers, under `resolution`.

resolution.description: texture resolution, e.g. 1k or 2k; omit for the material's default. A resolution the material does not carry is an error naming the ones it does — it is never silently swapped for another.

tools.name: search_assets
tools.description: SECOND ASSET RUNG: typed search over reusable HELIX Vault resources — call it before generating anything, and before looking at external/CC0 sources. Executes the packaged HELIX CLI and returns a COMPACT row per hit (id, title, kind, short description, format, size, performance tier, key dimensions, reuse counts, artifact + thumbnail URLs) — enough to choose. Bulk per-item `metadata` and `selectionExplanation` are omitted; get the full record for ONE asset with get_asset, its versions and checksums with list_asset_versions, or pass detail:true for the raw payload (large — it truncates). Prefer origin="generated" for trusted pipeline provenance and engine="web" for browser worlds. Ranking signals are independent — lexical match, hard filters, measured performance, observed reuse — never one magic score. Character rows carry skeleton (and skeletonVerification where the publish gate measured it): the browser runtime plays humanoid rigs, so a verified humanoid skeleton is what makes a character web-playable.

query.description: Full-text search over title, description, and tags

match.description: What the query DOES to the result set. "narrow" makes it a hard FILTER — use it to ask "does the Vault have X?", where an empty result is the honest answer. "recall" (the backend default when omitted) makes it a RANKING input over the whole library, so you always get the nearest candidates — use it to ask "show me candidates near X". Omitting this keeps recall, which never returns empty and will hand back confidently irrelevant rows when nothing real matches.

subtype.description: Typed subtype, e.g. static-prop or pbr-material

format.description: Primary format, e.g. glb, spz, hdr, or helix-material

engine.description: Runtime filter; usually "web" for Instant Worlds

official.description: TRUE narrows to the platform-vouched (official) tier — calibrated, convention-correct assets; try it FIRST for weapons and other interactive_item definitions, and widen only when it has no fit. FALSE narrows to community assets; omit for everything. A preference filter, never a gate.

detail.description: Return the CLI payload untrimmed, including per-item metadata and selectionExplanation. Large enough to be truncated at the default limit — prefer get_asset for one asset.

tools.name: search_vault
tools.description: THE CONTINUUM VAULT CATALOG — a different table from search_assets, and the ONLY discovery tool that finds LOOKS. `search_assets` hits the legacy raw-resource table, which has no Looks and never will; this hits `/api/v1/vault/catalog`, the table backing the website's Vault page, which lists every sealed, listed Continuum Package: Looks (pass packageType: "look"), characters, vehicles, weapons, devices, add-ons, materials. A LOOK (API identifier: `build`) is a free, never-owned dressed-character preset — its parts are still acquired individually from their own listings. Public: works signed out. Each hit that is a Look carries a compact `build` summary (its base and add-on slots); read the dressed character with model URLs and fit data via get_look, or the parts and prices via get_item_build.

query.description: Free-text search over title and tags

packageType.description: "look" is an alias for the API identifier "build" — use it to find Looks. Other Continuum Package types: character, vehicle, weapon, device, addon, material, animation, scene, gameplay, runtime-module, unreal-world, asset. Omit to search every type.

sort.description: Sort order; omit for the backend default

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous nextCursor

tools.name: search_items
tools.description: THE MARKETPLACE SHELF, not the Vault stockroom — and the only way to find a LOOK. `search_assets` searches raw creator RESOURCES (the meshes, clips and materials a world is built out of); this searches published PRODUCTS: what a creator has already finished, priced and listed. Two different tables answering two different questions, so reach for this one whenever the question is "has somebody already made this?" rather than "what parts exist?". A LOOK (API identifier: `build`) is a published, dressed-character (or vehicle/weapon/device) preset — a base plus the exact add-ons installed on it, pinned as an immutable Continuum Build Package — and it exists precisely so you do not have to reassemble it: for a police world, prefer a finished police character over sourcing a base, finding a uniform and proving the fit yourself. A LOOK IS NEVER OWNED ITSELF: it is a free, always-available preset, and its parts are still acquired individually from their own listings — applying one never grants, buys, or moves anything you do not already own. A Look is NOT its own category (a character Look IS an avatar, a vehicle Look IS a vehicle), so `builds` defaults to `include` and a plain query for "police" returns finished Looks alongside the parts. Every row carries `buildKind` when it is a Look — that field is the ONLY thing distinguishing a preset from the base it was assembled from. Inspect one with get_item_build for its part list and prices, or get_look for the dressed character (base + add-ons with model URLs) ready to render.

query.description: Free text over title, slug and tags

kind.description: Universal item kind: avatar, wearable, vehicle, weapon, add_on, home_item, home_shell, emote, prop

subCategory.description: Form factor beneath the category, e.g. car / plane / rifle / art

hostKind.description: Host class — vehicle / character / weapon. Answers both "add-ons for this class" and "things that TAKE add-ons".

builds.description: How much of the result is BUILDS. Omitted = `include` (the default): builds come back alongside the bases and parts, which is what makes a plain topical search find a finished preset. `only` narrows to presets — use it when you want something already assembled. `exclude` returns BASES to build on, which is what you want before publishing a build of your own.

tools.name: get_item_build
tools.description: WHAT IS IN A LOOK (API identifier: `build`): its base, every add-on installed on it, which of them you already own, and what the parts cost together. Call it on any item whose `buildKind` is set — search_items marks those — before deciding to use a preset, because a Look is a RECIPE and not a bundle: it is never owned itself, and its parts are still owned and bought individually, from their own listings, so `totalPriceLix` is the SUM of the parts rather than a price the Look itself charges. Answers 404 for an ordinary item, which is the normal case and not an error worth reporting. A part whose Continuum Package Version is not pinned to a marketplace item yet comes back with `item: null` and is counted in `unresolvedPartCount` — that part is genuinely in the Look and genuinely unavailable, so never read the remaining parts as the whole Look. For the dressed character itself — model URLs and fit data, ready to render, not just prices — use get_look instead.

itemId.description: Universal item id of the build (from search_items)

tools.name: get_look
tools.description: THE DRESSED CHARACTER BEHIND ONE LOOK, in a single public call: the base model plus every add-on, each with its pinned Continuum Package, model URL/CID, and the fit data the add-on composer needs (slot type, attach/skin mode, sealed fits/ops) — enough to reproduce the dressed character without any other call. Distinct from get_item_build, which lists parts and PRICES; this returns the ASSETS to render. Works signed out — public endpoint, no login required. `merged` is non-null only when the backend has composed a single merged Runtime Artifact (a stretch capability); when null, assemble base + addOns yourself with the engine's add-on composer. Identify the Look by its Universal Item id (from search_items / search_vault), or by its exact Package id and version.

itemId.description: Universal item id of the Look

packageId.description: Continuum Package id of the Look (use with version)

version.description: Package version; omitted defaults to the latest sealed version. Only meaningful with packageId

tools.name: save_look
tools.description: SAVE LOOK: freeze an inventory instance's CURRENT composition into a Look (a reusable, shareable, never-owned preset others can apply — never a copy others can own). Wraps the same authority as compose: never charges a publish fee, never grants a copy of any part to anyone, never creates a distribution. `visibility: 'private'` keeps it visible only to you; `'public'` seals a public Package plus Vault and Marketplace listings so others can discover and apply it (refused, with a readable reason, if any part lacks a Continuum pin or is not itself public). Pass `lookItemId` for a Look you already created to advance it to a new version instead of creating a new one — `created` in the result tells you which happened.

inventoryItemId.description: Inventory instance whose current composition becomes the Look

lookItemId.description: An existing Look you created — advances it to a new Package Version

tools.name: get_asset

tools.name: track_asset

tools.name: update_asset_metadata
tools.description: RETURNS A COMMAND, NOT DATA. This tool hands you a `helix …` command string to RUN yourself — it executes nothing and returns no results. The answer is in that command’s output. Update creator-owned Vault annotations only. Immutable artifact bytes, kind, skeleton, compatibility, and version are never mutated. Byte changes must enter through a sealed Continuum Package; direct Vault byte-first version uploads are retired.

tools.name: install_asset
tools.description: Resolve one durable Vault id, download the exact immutable version, verify server SHA-256 and byte count, then write public/helix.assets.json provenance. Material installs default to the lean runtime KTX2 family; request source for editable PNG maps or all only when both families are genuinely needed. The CLI owns rendition selection and installation. For reproducible installs, supply version, checksumSha256, and sizeBytes together. Any mismatch fails before a receipt is written.

directory.description: Absolute path to the world project root

sizeBytes.description: Expected byte size for that version

materialRenditions.description: Material map family: runtime KTX2 only (default), source PNG only, or all. Non-material assets are unchanged.

tools.name: start_asset_generation
tools.description: RETURNS A COMMAND, NOT DATA. This tool hands you a `helix …` command string to RUN yourself — it executes nothing and returns no results. The answer is in that command’s output. THE DURABLE ASYNC ROUTE — prefer it for every generation: it returns a job id immediately, so a timeout or a dropped connection never loses the job (poll it with poll_asset_generation instead of starting a duplicate). Covers all five generation surfaces. Prop/character route through main Dreamer; image/material/audio/Gaussian splat use the shared asset broker; animation delegates to the CLI’s explicit no-charge unavailable boundary. AUDIO: audioMode selects sound_effect (default), music, or text_to_speech — speech takes text + voiceId + languageCode from list_voices instead of a prompt. NEVER for vehicle sound (engine, exhaust, horn, doors, tyres, any one-shot): that is sourced from real recordings via import_vehicle_audio, not generated. COST IS NOT CAPPED BY THE ESTIMATE. The up-front quote is an estimate, and metered generations (audio in particular) settle on ACTUAL usage — the charge can land ABOVE or below it, and there is no automatic refund of a difference. A real music job quoted ~1.2 LIX settled at 1.4. To bound the spend, pass maxLix: the CLI refuses to start when the ESTIMATE exceeds it — that is a pre-flight guard on the quote, still not a guarantee about the final charge. Check what anything actually cost with `helix jobs`.

prompt.description: The generation prompt. Required for every kind EXCEPT audio in text_to_speech mode, which uses text instead.

loop.description: audio, sound_effect only: request a seamless loop

repeatPerMeter.description: material only: tile repeats per metre

maxLix.description: Refuse to start if the up-front ESTIMATE exceeds this many LIX. A guard on the quote, not a cap on the final metered charge.

audioMode.description: audio only: sound_effect (default), music, or text_to_speech

model.description: audio only: allowlisted model for the selected mode

outputFormat.description: audio only: portable MP3 rendition; defaults to mp3_44100_128

promptInfluence.description: audio, sound_effect only: prompt adherence from 0 to 1

text.description: audio, text_to_speech only: the spoken text (used INSTEAD of prompt)

voiceId.description: audio, text_to_speech only: a voice id returned by list_voices — never invent one

languageCode.description: audio, text_to_speech only: one of THAT voice's supported language codes

pronunciationDictionaryIds.description: audio, text_to_speech only: up to three unique provider dictionary ids

tools.name: poll_asset_generation
tools.description: RETURNS A COMMAND, NOT DATA. This tool hands you a `helix …` command string to RUN yourself — it executes nothing and returns no results. The answer is in that command’s output. Poll ONE known job without starting or advancing a duplicate. Successful asset-pipeline jobs report vaultAssetId plus vaultAutoPublish; main Dreamer jobs report the universal item id and Vault receipt after publish. A JOB THAT IS NOT DONE IS NOT NECESSARILY DEAD: a job can be PAUSED AT A GATE — waiting on the creator, or holding a concept the server itself rejected — and is still live and advanceable. When that is the case the status output carries the advance actions THE SERVER OFFERS for that job; read them from the response and use those. Never assume a fixed menu of recovery verbs and never infer one from this description — the server is the authority on what can advance a job, and it changes. DO NOT HAVE A JOB ID, OR WANT TO KNOW WHAT YOU SPENT? Run `helix jobs` — it lists your generation jobs with each one’s state and actual LIX cost, and prints the exact command that advances each parked job. `helix jobs --state unfinished` or `--state awaiting_approval` narrows it to what is stuck. That is the answer to "what did I spend" and "what is still waiting on me"; this tool is for a job you can already name.

pipeline.description: dreamer for prop/character; asset for all standalone kinds

tools.name: generate_image
tools.description: RETURNS A COMMAND, NOT DATA. This tool hands you a `helix …` command string to RUN yourself — it executes nothing and returns no results. The answer is in that command’s output. Generate a standalone image through the creator/client-token Dreamer API. This is NOT material generation. A successful default-on run includes a Vault asset id; explicit creator opt-out is returned as vaultAutoPublish="disabled". Spends the signed-in creator’s LIX — the up-front estimate is not a cap; `helix jobs` shows what it actually cost.

tools.name: generate_material
tools.description: RETURNS A COMMAND, NOT DATA. This tool hands you a `helix …` command string to RUN yourself — it executes nothing and returns no results. The answer is in that command’s output. Generate a validated portable PBR material bundle through the shared Dreamer asset pipeline and auto-publish it to Vault by default. Source PNG maps are retained; a KTX2 rendition is reported only when a real encoder produced it. 1K is the web/mobile default; 2K is explicit.

tools.name: list_voices
tools.description: List or search the authenticated HELIX text-to-speech voice catalog before generate_audio. Executes the packaged HELIX CLI and returns a COMPACT row per voice — id, name, category, short description, traits, and the deduped languageCodes you must pair the id with — plus a RECOMMENDED default that is guaranteed to have at least one language code. Per-language preview URLs are omitted (they were the bulk of the payload); pass detail:true for the raw catalog. Provider credentials, cloning, and voice administration are never exposed.

search.description: Search voice name, description, labels, and category

pageToken.description: Opaque next-page token returned by the preceding page

detail.description: Return the raw catalog response, including every per-language preview URL. Large.

tools.name: generate_audio
tools.description: Generate a sound effect, music track, or spoken line through the shared Dreamer audio pipeline, running the job to completion in ONE call. This executes the packaged HELIX CLI, which owns authentication, mode-specific validation, the long-running job, LIX accounting, provider access, and default-on Vault publication. Returns the CLI JSON receipt with the durable job/Vault ids and cost evidence. Sound effect is the default mode; music allows up to 4,100 prompt characters and 3-600 seconds; text_to_speech uses text + voiceId instead of prompt. NEVER use it for a vehicle: vehicle sound (engine, exhaust, horn, doors, tyres, any one-shot) is sourced from real recordings via import_vehicle_audio, never generated, and the vehicle gates refuse generated audio. PREFER start_asset_generation for anything slow: it also covers all three audio modes and hands back a job id, so a timeout or dropped connection cannot lose the job. AUDIO IS METERED — the charge settles on actual usage and can land above the estimate; there is no automatic refund. Check what it cost with `helix jobs`.

model.description: Allowlisted model for the selected mode; invalid mode/model pairs fail before generation.

tools.name: generate_asset
tools.description: RETURNS A COMMAND, NOT DATA. This tool hands you a `helix …` command string to RUN yourself — it executes nothing and returns no results. The answer is in that command’s output. LAST PLATFORM RUNG: generate a new prop or character only after list_materials and search_assets found no suitable resource. For a character, referenceSheetPath may supply an approved local FRONT/BACK/LEFT/RIGHT PNG/JPEG/WebP; the backend then skips image generation but preserves validation, mesh, texture, rig, LOD, thumbnail, billing, and Vault publication. This spends the signed-in creator’s LIX, and the up-front estimate is not a cap — `helix jobs` shows what each job actually cost. THIS COMMAND BLOCKS (default up to 20 minutes) waiting for the job — mesh generation on a complex prop can genuinely take a while. A "timed out" error is this wait giving up CLIENT-SIDE, not the job failing server-side: the printed `helix assets resume <job-id>` command checks on or continues that SAME job (never start a new one after a timeout). Pass timeoutMs to wait longer up front, or pollIntervalMs to poll less often.

referenceSheetPath.description: Character-only local path to a trusted FRONT/BACK/LEFT/RIGHT PNG, JPEG, or WebP sheet. Its exact bytes are checksum-bound and reused; no image generation is invoked.
